note: Gaze can be fed into VRChat from any program over Open Sound Control, at documented named addresses, in several formats — a pair of angles, angles plus a focus distance, direction vectors, or separate values per eye — plus a single closed-ness value driving both eyelids. VRChat states the sign conventions and the ten-second timeout after which it reverts to automatic looking. On the privacy side, VRChat requires the person to consent before it starts sending tracking data out to a discovered companion program. The flow is inbound: outside programs push gaze into VRChat, and VRChat publishes no general gaze feed back out.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Touch feedback is felt when it is missing, and nothing stops.
note: A world script can vibrate a person's controller in a chosen hand, giving duration, strength and speed as three values from zero to one. There is no richer haptic description and nothing for gloves or suits beyond whatever their driver reports as a controller.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A world that cannot ask what the arriving device can do will guess, and guessing wrong costs quality rather than entry.
note: A creator can learn a useful amount about the person's setup: whether they are in a headset, and a single number saying whether they are on a desktop computer, using hands only, head and hands, or four, five or six tracked points. There is no general capability list — no way to ask about eye tracking, hand tracking, haptics, refresh rate or display.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: The language a world writes its rules in is its own business and never has to cross.
note: World rules are written in Udon, which is VRChat's own language running on VRChat's own bytecode interpreter. Creators usually write a restricted dialect of C# which the tool compiles down to Udon assembly, and VRChat states plainly that this dialect follows no version of the C# standard. Generic classes, interfaces, method overloads and properties do not work. The compiled program only runs inside VRChat and can never be moved to another runtime. The compiler itself is open source under a permissive licence, which is a real positive, but it only ever emits VRChat bytecode.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: The use case says the asset must behave, so a door that will not open in the second system is the failure this row names.
note: VRChat has a visual node graph for interactivity, which sounds like the portable declarative behaviour other systems are converging on — but it is not. The graph compiles in the background into the same VRChat-only assembly as everything else, so the interactivity does not travel with an asset; it is baked into a proprietary bytecode blob inside a Unity asset bundle.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A host can sandbox guest content on its own; agreement only makes the limits predictable for the guest.
note: This is VRChat's strongest capability. Guest content cannot run arbitrary code: worlds and avatars may only use components from two published closed allowlists, anything else is refused at upload, and all scripting goes through the interpreter rather than the host runtime. Reaching the network is gated by an address allowlist that a person must deliberately override. On top of that sits the trust and shield system that decides how much of a stranger's avatar to render at all.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: An agent with no agreed way to perceive and act in a world it did not come from cannot join it at all.
note: Autonomous characters are supported through Unity's navigation meshes, including building and updating them while the world is running, with some capabilities held back. There is no notion of an external autonomous agent joining a world as a participant, and no interface for one.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Without agreed limits, guest content and agents are throttled or refused unpredictably.
note: VRChat publishes hard numbers for almost everything guest content may consume, which is rare and valuable. Network traffic is capped per script and per update. Events are rate limited with a default and a ceiling. Downloads are throttled to one every five seconds with size and resolution caps. Avatars have download and in-memory size caps per platform. On top of that the performance rank system turns the whole avatar budget into a single score that viewers can filter on.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: What survives a restart is mostly the host's business; it crosses the boundary only when a visitor's changes must last.
note: What survives is per-person, not per-world. Each visitor gets a key-value store belonging to that world, and can be given their own copy of an object whose shared values are saved. So scores, unlocks, currency and preferences come back. What does not come back is the state of the world's own furniture — there is no documented way to restart an instance and find shared world objects where they were left. VRChat also warns data must be written before the person leaves.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: The use case names inventory, and items that cannot be read at the destination do not travel with the person.
note: Worlds can and do keep inventories, but they never travel. VRChat states outright that saved data cannot be shared between worlds, so an item earned in one world does not exist in the next. The separate spawnable-object feature is not an inventory at all — VRChat says scripts cannot even see those objects, and that a script which tries to handle one will throw and disable itself.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: The use case names preferences, and for a person who depends on comfort and accessibility settings, arriving without them ends the visit.
note: Client-level settings do follow the person everywhere in VRChat — safety shields, the avatar-quality limits they will accept, and per-person interaction overrides that VRChat says are kept between sessions. Anything a world stores about a person's preferences stays in that world. Nothing follows a person to another operator.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Naming content by hash makes an item the same item everywhere; without it copies drift while still loading.
note: Content is referred to by location and registry entry, never by hash. Worlds and avatars are named by identifiers that VRChat's servers resolve, and no page checked mentions addressing an asset by its content digest.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A runnable experience moves between hosts far less often than an asset does, and repackaging is the fallback.
note: The runnable package is a Unity asset bundle, compiled per platform, tied to a single pinned Unity editor version, and readable only by a matching VRChat client. Three platforms mean three separate builds and three separate uploads under one identifier. This is the opposite of a portable package format: nothing outside VRChat can open it, run it, inspect it or convert it.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Assets reach clients over ordinary web delivery, so agreement here buys scale and cost rather than possibility.
note: VRChat hosts and serves the content itself, choosing the right platform build for whichever client asks. Creators do not choose a host, cannot self-host a world, and get no delivery controls. VRChat also runs a media host that appears on the allowed address list for streams and files.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A reader that cannot tell which version it holds, or what to do with the parts it does not know, breaks on the first update, which is the "no hand fixes" test again.
note: Shipping a change routinely breaks things, and VRChat says so. Moving to a different Unity editor version stops uploaded content loading at all. Separately, adding a component or a shared variable to a networked object makes the new build incompatible with instances already running the old one, and people joining those instances are warned. VRChat ships a whole tool whose only job is to keep numeric object identifiers stable across builds, because if they drift, people see different objects receiving each other's data.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Every other must row is a claim until a shared test says it holds, which is exactly what the meeting asked for.
note: There is testing, but it proves conformance to VRChat rather than to any specification. The upload tool validates content against VRChat's rules, and a simulator in the editor reproduces much of the client so creators can test before uploading. VRChat is explicit that the simulator cannot cover everything and that real testing must happen in the product. Since there is no specification for anyone else to implement, there is nothing external to conform to.

subject: VRChat
capability: World generation from a prompt or an image
interop_reason: A generated place that arrives only as frames to watch still reaches the viewer, but as a recording rather than a world the receiver can open and use.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and making a whole three-dimensional place from a description or a picture is not an act it performs or specifies.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A world continued by a model still reaches a viewer, but only as what the model chooses to show, so the receiver cannot keep it or run it again.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it never continues a world under a viewer's actions from a learned model; there is no such model here.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: How a system turns photographs into a model is its own method, and what leaves is an ordinary asset the container and geometry rows already carry.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and turning a set of ordinary photographs into a textured three-dimensional model is not among its jobs.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so this row is what geometry encoding is for a mesh: splat content in a named format the receiving tool cannot read does not arrive at all, and re-exporting it is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: The list of components a world may contain is closed and holds no splat renderer, and a creator cannot add one because custom engine code does not run in worlds. So a splat file has nothing to load it and nothing to draw it.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what arrives first, a large capture still loads, it just makes the viewer wait for the whole of it.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it delivers no captured scene, progressively by region and detail or otherwise.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a volumetric clip is an asset like any other: without the calibration and mask metadata a second implementation needs, what arrives is not the recording and no one can make it one by hand.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it carries no captured, time-varying three-dimensional scene as media, and no camera calibration or mask metadata for one.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a point cloud encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a point cloud, exactly as an undecodable mesh is not a mesh, and that capture shows nothing.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it defines no encoding or compression for a set of points with attributes.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so views that arrive without their intrinsics and extrinsics cannot be reprojected: the capture lands as loose pictures rather than as the place it recorded.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it carries no set of calibrated camera views with per-pixel depth, and no intrinsics or extrinsics to reproject them.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Making an image from a viewpoint no camera occupied is a method inside one system, and what crosses to a second system is the picture it produced.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it produces no image from a viewing position that no capture camera occupied.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a moving capture handed over as unrelated frames is not the capture: the receiver has to guess the rate and the ordering the sender already knew, and guessing is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it carries no captured scene that changes over time, and states no rate at which one should be played back.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Whether a captured scene answers the light around it is work the receiving system does, and the asset arrives either way.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it holds no captured scene that could be made to answer the light of the place it lands in.

subject: VRChat
capability: Editing a capture after the fact
interop_reason: Editing a capture happens in the tool that holds it, and what leaves is the edited asset, which the format rows already carry.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and there is no capture here to crop, delete from or recolour, and no export for such an edit to survive.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Describing a change to a world you already made is one service's own interface, and the world that results still leaves by the ordinary export rows.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and there is no generated world here to change by describing the change or pointing at a region.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A generator that cannot read the specification another tool wrote still produces a world, it just will not be the world that was asked for.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and nothing here accepts a specification of a world that should be made.

subject: VRChat
capability: Deriving conventional assets from a generated scene
interop_reason: Derived meshes and panoramas are how a generated world reaches a conventional engine at all, and each route loses something the receiver has to be told about.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it derives no collision mesh, drawing mesh, panorama or video from a splat or radiance-field world.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Actions that arrive without their embodiment, frame and units cannot be replayed elsewhere, so an agent acts only in the system it was written for.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it carries no agent's actions in or out as time-sampled data with an embodiment, a frame and units.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A panorama whose projection is not stated is still an image, but the receiver has to guess before it can use it as a backdrop or as a light.
note: VRChat is a hosted platform whose world contents are drawn from a closed list of allowed components, and it carries no full 360-degree view of a place as an image with its projection stated.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A reconstruction that cannot leave the device that made it keeps the room private to one session, so anything placed against it has to be fitted again elsewhere.
note: Worlds are authored in Unity and uploaded; the components a world may use are an enumerated allowlist, and no reconstruction, plane or room component appears in it. The real room is not part of what a VRChat world can see.

subject: VRChat
capability: Semantic labelling of the real world
interop_reason: Labels each vendor names differently still serve one application, but a second one cannot act on floor or sky without being rewritten for that vendor.
note: There is no channel through which a world learns what a real surface is, because there is no real surface in its model. Labelling in VRChat applies to avatar parameters and world objects the creator made.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Depth reported in units the receiver does not share puts real surfaces at the wrong distance, so content is placed badly rather than not at all.
note: No camera image and no depth of the physical world reaches world logic. The allowlist that defines what a world may run carries nothing that would deliver one.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Whether real surfaces hide virtual content is drawn on the device that sees them, and none of that decision crosses to a second system.
note: Worlds are drawn as fully virtual scenes. With no passthrough view and no real-world depth, there is nothing for content to be hidden behind.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: How much of the real room a runtime lets through is its own presentation, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.
note: What a world author can set about presentation is spawn points, spawn order, camera reference and the layers interaction may pass through — the word passthrough in VRChat's documentation means interaction passing through a layer, not the camera view of the room. No published world setting or component blends a live camera image with the world. Absence read off the world documentation rather than a statement by VRChat, so it is recorded unverified.

subject: VRChat
capability: Face and body tracking as input
interop_reason: A face and body stream in a shape the receiver does not read leaves the avatar still rather than absent, and its privacy terms have to be agreed with it.
note: The person's own movement does arrive as a live stream, over Open Sound Control rather than from a headset driver: gaze at documented addresses, and tracker positions and rotations fed into the full body inverse kinematics. It is half the row — body pose and eyes yes, a full facial expression stream only as far as an outside program chooses to send avatar parameters — and the privacy terms are a notification that an application is sending data, not an agreed constraint.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A place that arrives without its walkable surface and arrival points still loads, but whoever opens it has to work out where a body may stand and where a portal lands.
note: Arrival is carried with the world and the walkable surface is not. The scene descriptor holds an array of spawn transforms with a radius and an order, so a world says where visitors land; the navigable surface is a Unity navigation mesh built by the author and now buildable at run time, which stays inside VRChat's own Unity project and never travels as a declaration anyone else could read.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A published unit of logic whose name resolves to something else elsewhere still runs, but nobody can be sure which code they called.
note: World logic is compiled into the world's own build. Nothing is published as a unit of logic under a name another author resolves, so there is no namespace to be permanent and no claim to protect.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiving world that cannot tell what review arriving content has already had still shows it, and has to repeat the whole review itself.
note: There is a real gate and it is a staged audience rather than a review: a world made public goes first to Community Labs, immediately visible to the users who opt into it, and reaches everyone later. Judgement is after the fact — content violating the guidelines costs the author the ability to submit and can bring moderation action — and nothing about what review a world or its assets have had travels with them to another system.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Two maps of one place with no published transform between them put the same content in two positions, so a person arrives beside where they meant to be.
note: VRChat's creator documentation presents worlds as custom spaces that people create and visit, built in Unity. A world is an invented place, so there is no map of a real place to declare and nothing to align it to.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A service that never declares where it applies still answers, so a client has to call it and find out instead of testing whether it is relevant.
note: VRChat's creator documentation presents worlds as custom spaces that people create and visit, built in Unity. A world is not bound to a region of the Earth and declares no area where it applies.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiver must distinguish required additions from optional ones or it cannot safely interpret an arriving asset or exchange.
note: Udon scripts and SDK components are the declared way to add behaviour, but only from a closed list that VRChat controls, and there is no named, versioned extension registry. The only stated rule for a recipient that lacks a feature is the shader fallback tag.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Named subsets make compatible requirements easier to select, while systems can still agree on the individual requirements without a named profile.
note: VRChat publishes named levels with stated limits: the five performance ranks and a separate Android content limit set. They are VRChat's own and computed by VRChat; content does not declare a profile, and no second implementation can claim one.

subject: VRChat
capability: Domain metadata carried with an asset
interop_reason: An asset can load without shared descriptive properties, but receivers lose the classifications and facts that drive its use.
note: A world carries a scene descriptor with fixed fields (spawns, respawn height, interaction rules). Listing details such as tags are entered on the website and stored on VRChat's servers, not in the asset, and no declared schema lets another system read them.

subject: VRChat
capability: Assurance and evidence behind a claim
interop_reason: A credential can be presented without shared assurance detail, but the receiver has less evidence for deciding whether to trust it.
note: Age verification is done with a third-party ID and selfie check, and viewers see a shield or badge that tells them the check was passed. The method and evidence are described only in help text and do not travel with the claim for a relying party to assess.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiving world cannot use a credential reliably unless it can interpret the claim vocabulary and check its structure.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for schema, vocabulary, claim type, credential, attestation, verifiable on 2026-10-20; found no declared vocabulary or validation schema for any claim. The one claim about a person, age verification, is a feature of VRChat's own client and servers.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Travel can continue with reusable identifiers, but correlating visits across relationships creates a privacy loss.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for pairwise, pseudonym, unlinkable, correlate, user ID on 2026-10-20; found no per-relationship identifiers. One account identifier is used everywhere and is embedded in photo metadata.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A moved asset remains usable without a shared preview image, but selection and arrival previews become slower or less informative.
note: Published worlds include a separate preview image in their metadata.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Travel and participation can use a shared session without encrypted subject payloads, but lack of agreement prevents confidential subject data from following safely.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for encrypt, end-to-end, recipient key, public key, TLS on 2026-10-20; found no way to name a recipient's key or deliver content encrypted for one person. Purchased content is gated by VRChat's own entitlement records.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: After identity keys change, a destination must find the applicable verification material to recognize the same person or agent safely.
note: Account sign-in has a stated recovery route: second-factor recovery codes let a person log in after losing the authenticator. There are no rules for rotating or revoking keys, and no verification material is published for anyone else to discover.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A destination cannot rely on an issued credential for admission or authority unless the agreed mechanism lets it discover that the credential has been withdrawn.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for revoke, revocation, expire, status list, re-verify on 2026-10-20; found no mechanism for anyone but VRChat to check the standing of an age-verification claim after it was issued; other users see only a badge.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A scene or visit can continue when interface layouts differ, but carried controls and information may become hard to use.
note: VRC Ui Shape exposes scene Canvas interfaces that players can point at, click and scroll.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: An asset with external resources cannot load intact if the receiver cannot resolve its resource references in the intended context.
note: VRChat resolves world and avatar blueprint identifiers on its own servers, and resolves video, string and image URLs at run time. Domains on VRChat's allowlist load for everyone; other domains load only when the viewer enables "Allow Untrusted URLs" in their settings, and in public instances a world's video player also needs the domain added to the world's own allowed list. A world cannot reference an outside asset by identifier and have a resolver fetch it.

subject: VRChat
capability: Pose series and live pose streams
interop_reason: Systems exchanging moving subjects must agree on the time and frame of each pose or the subject's movement cannot be reconstructed correctly.
note: A program can stream up to eight tracker poses into VRChat over OSC, as positions and euler angles on named addresses, and VRChat sends the head and wrist poses of the VR system out over OSC together with an OSC bundle timestamp. The pages read declare no interpolation rule for either stream, and neither is described as an interchange form for a pose sequence.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Turning local pointing input into a scene hit stays inside the receiving application and does not require agreement between independent worlds.
note: VRCRaycast positions a transform at a scene hit; the captured component does not alone prove returning the intersected object or geometry to application code.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Receiving text through a local input field or keyboard interface is a device-side interaction and need not be shared between worlds.
note: TMP_InputField exposes editable text with value and focus state for world interfaces.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Shared bounds let a receiver select content before loading its geometry; without them the content can still move but loads and traverses less efficiently.
note: Worlds can use Unity occlusion culling, which relies on baked visibility volumes to reject hidden geometry. The data is baked into the opaque uploaded bundle and VRChat documents no bounding-volume format for another tool to read.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Losing agreed object sets weakens grouped scene operations while the individual objects can still be transferred and rendered.
note: Unity layers act as named sets that scene operations target, such as which layers a mirror reflects or which layers pass interaction, and VRChat's layers page lists them by name. The missing part is that they are a fixed table of 32 layers numbered 0 to 31, several reserved by VRChat (objects on a reserved layer are moved to Layer 0 on upload), and no set can be defined by a rule.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A moved object or avatar can still load when constraints are lost, but linked movement and pose behavior degrade.
note: VRChat's custom constraints define relative transform behavior for avatars and worlds.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A scene can transfer without agreed media timing, but its video, sound and coordinated presentation can be lost or drift.
note: The supplied synchronized video-player prefabs coordinate chosen videos for participants in a world; the example's loop limitation is explicit.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiver cannot access protected transferred content unless it can identify the protection mechanism required for that content.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for protection, DRM, copy protection, encrypt, watermark, obfuscate, ripping on 2026-10-20; found no way to declare a protection scheme on an uploaded world, avatar or component. The only related control is the avatar cloning switch, which is a permission and names no scheme.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Without agreed links and transform meaning, receivers cannot reconstruct the same related frames for transferred content or participants.
note: VRChat takes up to eight tracker poses in one OSC tracking space and shifts that space so the head pose aligns with the avatar's head, but the poses are separate and unlinked, and no chain, parent link or graph of related frames is described for interchange; avatar and world transform hierarchies exist only inside the uploaded Unity bundle. Searched all 311 pages of creators.vrchat.com in its sitemap, ten OSC pages of docs.vrchat.com and the OSCQuery wiki page for pose graph, kinematic chain, transform graph, frame graph, pose chain, linked pose, coordinate frame, reference frame, frames of reference, parent frame and transform tree on 2026-10-20; the only match is the words transform tree inside a list of allowed Unity components. The remaining docs.vrchat.com pages were not searched.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A recipient that cannot interpret the carried permission cannot determine whether the requested use of the subject or data is authorized.
note: Some permissions are switches the person controls and can withdraw, such as allowing others to clone a public avatar. They are account settings held by VRChat, not a grant that travels with the avatar with a stated purpose and validity period.

subject: VRChat
capability: Record of what a system decided
interop_reason: A shared evaluation receipt makes cross-system actions auditable, while travel or participation can still occur without that record.
note: When a viewer's client declines to show an avatar, the viewer sees a fallback avatar and a stated reason, such as the avatar not being available for their platform. This is a human-readable outcome on screen, not a machine-readable record with any signature.

subject: VRChat
capability: Deciding whether to admit an arrival
interop_reason: A traveller or agent cannot safely complete entry unless the origin and destination understand the destination's approval, refusal and validity conditions.
note: Instance privacy levels decide whether a person may join: in an Invite instance a join request must be approved by the host. The documentation defines no refusal response with a validity limit or an explanation field.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot evaluate the transmitted curves and surfaces cannot reconstruct an asset whose geometry is carried in that form.
note: The only curve evaluated from mathematical form is the Catmull-Rom spline path of VRCTween, a motion path set up by script. Worlds are otherwise triangle meshes, and no parametric surfaces are carried.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Losing an exchanged emitter's parameters removes or changes visual effects while the containing asset or avatar can still arrive.
note: VRChat's world-component allowlist explicitly supports the named Unity ParticleSystem, ParticleSystemRenderer and force-field components in uploaded worlds. These are the authored Unity emitter/effect route evaluated by the client.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A stripped provenance record weakens trust in an arriving asset while the asset remains usable.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for watermark, fingerprint, provenance, C2PA, content credentials, digital signature on 2026-10-20; no match. The only link from an asset to its maker is the blueprint identifier held in VRChat's database, so there is no embedded record to lose and no fingerprint route to recover one.

subject: VRChat
capability: Declarative styling carried apart from the content
interop_reason: Without shared styling rules, a moved scene can still load while its metadata-driven visibility and appearance change.
note: Appearance in a VRChat world is set through each object's materials, shaders and layers, and scripts can change material properties at run time, so display styling is within what a world does; no separate rule set that selects features by metadata and changes colour or visibility is described. Searched all 311 pages of creators.vrchat.com in its sitemap for style rule, styling, stylesheet, style sheet, restyle, per-feature, metadata-driven and conditional style on 2026-10-20; no match. docs.vrchat.com and the VRChat help centre were not searched for this row.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A default asset can arrive when variant selection is lost, but the chosen configuration of the asset or avatar changes.
note: The SDK uploads platform-specific avatar versions under one ID; this is platform selection, not a general named asset-configuration selection contract.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot decode the exchanged cells and their properties cannot reconstruct content represented as a voxel volume.
note: Searched creators.vrchat.com (all 311 pages in its sitemap), docs.vrchat.com (345 pages reached from its index and release notes) and the VRChat help centre (84 articles) for voxel, voxels on 2026-10-20; no match. Unity Grid, Tilemap and Terrain components are allowed, but none carries a volume of cells with properties for exchange.

subject: VRChat
interop_reason: Without an agreed musical-event interface, an arriving performance or interactive experience loses instrument input while other interaction paths remain.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: The file is the boundary: if the second system cannot open it, nothing else on this list matters.

note: The pinned Forum Sneeze glTF loader reads scene nodes with local transforms and child indices from glTF/GLB and composes children under their parent transform.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Travel and participation can continue without shared zone-event meaning, but spatial notifications and summaries lose useful context.
note: No zone or event interchange exists: nodes carry bounding extents but no trigger or zone type, and the module interface delivers only timer events. The architecture describes fabric-defined audio and video zones as regions in the scene object model, which is a plan with no format. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for zone, event, trigger, region, geofence and Notify on 2026-10-20; the only zone hits are the proposal's safety and A/V zones and the clock-zone setting in the time API.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A recipient that cannot interpret the carried permission cannot determine whether the requested use of the subject or data is authorized.
note: No grant of permission is carried with anything: there is no scope, purpose, validity or withdrawal record, and the engine's persona is a typed local name. The architecture proposes that services request capabilities and the user grants or denies, and that agreement to terms is recorded as a signed acknowledgment, but calls the design of consent an area needing significant community input. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for consent, grant, permission, acknowledgment, withdraw and terms of service on 2026-10-20; found only the proposal's descriptions.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
capability: Record of what a system decided
interop_reason: A shared evaluation receipt makes cross-system actions auditable, while travel or participation can still occur without that record.
note: The separate Sneeze SDK/MSF module exposes machine-readable signature and certificate trust results. The retained passage does not define an acceptance/rejection/action receipt from a relying recipient.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Choosing and dispatching internal GPU computation does not require agreement between the systems that exchange an asset.
note: The pinned Forum engine compute module dispatches SPIR-V kernels through Vox; guest SDK exposure is not established.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
capability: Frame pacing and predicted display time
interop_reason: Disagreement between an arriving application and the device runtime about display timing degrades the view through stale poses or poor frame pacing.
note: No display timing is used: a window surface is presented at a fixed 60 frames a second and the XR module only reports whether a runtime exists, so there is no predicted display time and no view pose tied to one. The architecture names frame timing as part of OpenXR rendering submission. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac), the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) and the Halogen README for frame timing, predicted display time, xrWaitFrame, vsync and view pose on 2026-10-20; the only hits are the proposal and the SDK's note that the monotonic clock suits frame pacing.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: An asset can still load with fallback materials when its shaders are not understood, but authored appearance degrades.
note: The engine takes SPIR-V as its shader format for compute: kernels compiled from GLSL at build time are dispatched through a graphics-compute layer, and SPIR-V from remote content must pass validation against the Vulkan compute profile first. Missing is any path for visual shaders, any field in the fabric or node record that carries a shader, and any statement of how a fabric would deliver a kernel, so only embedded kernels are in use.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot evaluate the transmitted curves and surfaces cannot reconstruct an asset whose geometry is carried in that form.
note: The architecture fixes glTF, a mesh format, as the only delivery format at the browser boundary and says exact-geometry sources such as building-model and USD data are converted before they reach the browser, so carrying curves and surfaces in mathematical form is not what this browser does.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Losing an exchanged emitter's parameters removes or changes visual effects while the containing asset or avatar can still arrive.
note: No emitter or particle system exists in the node model or the renderer. The architecture expects particle effects to come from custom shaders shipped with content, which the engine has no path to receive. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for particle, emitter, effect and simulation parameters on 2026-10-20; the hits are the proposal's mentions of particle trails and particle-driven appearances and an unrelated geometry-emitter remark in the UI working note.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A stripped provenance record weakens trust in an arriving asset while the asset remains usable.
note: Provenance travels only inside the signed wrapper: the manifest is a signed envelope, and if the signature or its certificate chain is stripped the content cannot be traced back, since there is no fingerprint registry or watermark lookup. The architecture covers signing and a chain from code to publisher, not recovery. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for watermark, content credentials, C2PA, perceptual hash, fingerprint lookup and provenance on 2026-10-20; the fingerprint hits are all signing-certificate fingerprints.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A default asset can arrive when variant selection is lost, but the chosen configuration of the asset or avatar changes.
note: No selectable variants exist: the glTF loader reads only the default scene, lists the extensions it enables, and does not include the glTF material-variants extension, and the fabric format has no alternative-configuration field. The architecture names glTF as the delivery format at the browser boundary. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for variant, KHR_materials_variants, alternative, configuration and selection on 2026-10-20.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A receiver that cannot decode the exchanged cells and their properties cannot reconstruct content represented as a voxel volume.
note: No cell volume is exchanged: the node record has no voxel type, the renderer has no volume subtype, and the glTF loader maps only triangles. The architecture lists volumes among the objects its rendering abstraction handles. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for voxel, volume, cell, grid and spatial field on 2026-10-20; found no voxel structure.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
capability: Hit test against the real world
interop_reason: A disagreement about sensing hit results makes placement and interaction worse, while manual placement can keep the experience usable.
note: No query against the physical surroundings exists: the engine has no sensing interface and a guest module cannot even pick virtual content. The architecture places scene understanding in OpenXR extensions rather than defining a ray query. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for hit test, ray cast, raycast, plane detection and surface intersection on 2026-10-20; found no real-world query.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Without shared sensed-data disclosure terms, content, avatars, travellers and agents can still operate but may expose more data than intended.
note: No disclosure control exists on sensed data, because no sensed data reaches the engine. The architecture proposes that services never receive raw sensor data by default and that the browser grants only the minimum, with no coarsening, retention or pseudonymous-publication terms defined. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac) and the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) for sensor, raw data, coarsening, retention, minimum necessary and pseudonymous pose on 2026-10-20; found only the proposal's section on sensor permissions.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Without an agreed musical-event interface, an arriving performance or interactive experience loses instrument input while other interaction paths remain.
note: The architecture has the browser route input from whatever device the user has, so a device interface is in scope, but nothing defines musical events: the input described is XR hardware reached through OpenXR actions. Searched the Sneeze architecture proposal 2026.Q2.0 (SneezeDoc commit 8e26da5) and its overview pages, the SneezeSDK prep documentation and C header (commit 4239e2b), the Forum Sneeze README and module notes (commit 04bc0ac), the MetaversalCorp Sneeze README and module notes (commit 986fc4c) and the RCSF documents (commit f6c3ea8) for MIDI, musical and instrument on 2026-10-20; the only hits are the word humidity (matching MIDI as a substring) and a network instrumentation counter, so no typed musical-event interface exists.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: The fitting method stays inside the capture tool, while the resulting field crosses through the separate representation and format capabilities.
note: The browser's stated job is to maintain, connect, execute and render a scene, and training a radiance field or Gaussian representation from images is an offline production step that happens before content reaches a browser.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: The generation method stays inside one tool, while its placeable output travels through the ordinary asset and representation capabilities.
note: The browser's stated job is to maintain, connect, execute and render a scene, and producing an object from a text or image prompt is authoring work done by tools or services whose output arrives as glTF at the browser boundary.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: If two systems disagree on what a contained experience may do, the containment either fails or becomes a security hole; there is no partial agreement that works.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser loads and displays spatial content from multiple formats, with native scene composition. It can host content from different sources within a unified viewport. But it is a browser that navigates between content, not a runtime that hosts one experience's running logic inside another with defined containment boundaries and an event propagation protocol.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A coupling that carries change without anyone crossing needs both ends to agree on authority, ordering and settlement, or the two worlds silently diverge.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser navigates between spatial content and has some networking for session joining. But it does not define a mechanism for state in one loaded world to cause changes in another world with nobody present. Its role is displaying content, not coupling world state.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: The agent use case says an agent pays for what it uses; if payer and payee share no payment exchange, the payment cannot happen at all.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser is a client that presents credentials to services, and its architecture has a payment service receiving payment authorization, so payment is within its scope, but the browser defines no payment requirements, authorization or settlement. Searched Sneeze architecture at 8e26da5 and Rubidium README at fd8f6be for payment, commerce, settle, wallet, purchase on 2026-10-20; payment appears only as a service receiving authorization (wallet only for identity credentials), no exchange defined.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
capability: Entitlements and licence checks at use
interop_reason: A destination that cannot read a grant must refuse the item, the entry or the agent, or admit it blindly.
note: The browser's architecture assigns commerce to services run by each fabric's owner, outside the browser; its scene branch ownership controls who may write to the scene, not whether a holder has a grant to a resource.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A grant can still be checked with its issuer without a portable receipt, but a third system cannot verify the purchase on its own.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser is a client for opening spatial content; any purchase or grant record would come from a store or credential system it displays, not from the browser.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Credentials still verify without a shared registry, but each receiver must decide alone whom to trust, so acceptance differs from world to world.
note: The engine checks a fabric's signature and certificate chain against the operating system's root store; that is roots alone and does not choose which publishers or worlds a verifier accepts. Searched SneezeDoc trust-and-isolation.md and sneeze-architecture.md (commit 8e26da5) and Sneeze MsfFile.md and Persona.md (commit 986fc4c) for registry, allow-list, trust list, publisher, issuer and trust anchor on 2026-10-20; the architecture mentions a DID registry and a service registry of module hashes, but none defines governed acceptance of publishers or worlds.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: An agent can still build in each platform through that platform's own interface, but without a shared one every agent needs a separate integration for every platform.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser is a client for opening spatial content, so its purpose is viewing rather than offering an outside agent a way to build and publish; the fabric signing tool in its engine repository is scored under RP1.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Assets can still move one at a time, but a place that cannot leave its host as a whole has to be rebuilt by hand when the host changes or closes.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser is a client that connects to fabrics served elsewhere; the place lives with the fabric's services, so exporting a whole place is not something the browser does.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: The object model arrives from another system, so its format and units must be readable by the tracker, while the tracking itself stays on the device.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser engine reaches XR devices through OpenXR, so device-side sensing is not excluded, but the documents read describe no object tracking. Searched the Sneeze README (commit 986fc4c) and the Rubidium README (main branch as read) for object track, object recogn, marker, image track, tracking, ARKit, ARCore and camera on 2026-10-20; the only hits were OpenXR device access, a branch-tracking build term and the rendering camera, and the engine source and further documentation were not searched.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Recorded descriptively by the owner's decision of 2026-09-18: the Atlas records which systems render remotely and does not define an agreement between client and renderer.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser's engine draws the scene locally into a surface the host application supplies, and its architecture streams scene updates, not rendered frames.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: A digital twin can still be shown without a shared binding, but each data source must be wired by hand; the Atlas's four use cases do not yet include digital twins, so the row is recorded against content that moves.
note: The browser's architecture runs sandboxed services with their own backends, and its own example is a service that turns ceiling-sensor readings into a live heat map. This is described as a use of the service model; services reach their backends through RMAP model objects with properties, events and actions, but no binding from a backend to a sensor or controller, and no controller write-back, is specified.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Training still finishes without a portable record, but the result stays in one vendor's dashboard instead of travelling with the person.
note: The Open Metaverse Browser architecture covers how a browser engine connects to fabrics and services and renders them; recording what a person did and with what result would be done by a service, and the architecture defines no such record.

subject: Open Metaverse Browser
interop_reason: Sensors and experiences come from different vendors; without a shared signal description each adaptation is wired to one device, though the experience still runs without it.
note: Searched SneezeDoc at commit 8e26da5, Sneeze at commit 986fc4c, the Forum Sneeze engine (MetaverseStandards/Sneeze) at commit 04bc0ac, SneezeSDK at commits 4239e2b and 44d0346 and Rubidium at commit 3b8a68e, all text files, for heart rate, galvanic, skin conductance, physiolog, biometric, biosignal, electrodermal, biofeedback and wearable on 2026-10-20; no match in documentation or source. The engine's user input is position, orientation and device tracking; its OpenXR module only detects a runtime.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: How a system turns geometry into pixels never leaves that system, so two runtimes can draw the same scene by different means and nothing crosses.
note: The engine abstracts drawing behind a rendering interface rather than fixing a pipeline, so the pass structure belongs to whichever device is loaded. The earlier statement that the pipeline cannot be inspected no longer holds: the engine, its rendering device and the browser all have public repositories, and the engine's dependency manifest now clones both formerly private libraries from public addresses. The licence picture is uneven and matters to a working group: the engine and the interface SDK are Apache-2.0, the browser's own README calls it proprietary with all rights reserved, and the map library ships no licence file at all.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: The graphics interface a runtime targets is a build choice inside one system, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.
note: The renderer is written against ANARI, with the Halogen backend on Filament; Filament creates a Vulkan swapchain on Windows and runs its Metal backend on macOS, and the architecture document says application code never calls a graphics API directly.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: An asset that arrives against a different surface model still loads, but the further apart the two models are the more the look drifts.
note: Surfaces are described by glTF metallic-roughness factors and maps, alpha modes, double-sidedness, unlit and a bounded MToon translation, and the renderer evaluates them with Halogen's physically based material. Missing: transmission is skipped with a blended fallback, compressed-texture maps stay empty, and no other material model is carried.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A moved scene whose lights are read differently is lit wrong rather than lost.
note: Lighting is now documented in public. Scene-wide ambient and directional light are authored in the manifest's Primary block and are scene properties, not nodes, so a local object cannot alter global illumination; placed point and spot lights are ordinary nodes carrying colour, intensity and cone angles. The composition rule the integration once had to derive from source is now stated: a placed light's intensity is multiplied by the square of its world scale times the scene's flattening scale. There is no indirect light, no shadow model and no probe model anywhere in the format.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Effects applied after the main pass are the receiving system's taste and carry nothing across.
note: Searched the public RP1 repositories at their main heads on 2026-10-20 - Sneeze (986fc4c), Rubidium (3b8a68e), SneezeDoc (8e26da5), SneezeSDK (44d0346), RMAP (0fd7efb) and Map (0e6d26a), all text files including source and the architecture document, for post-processing, bloom, tone mapping, SSAO and anti-aliasing. The backend applies a fixed post-processing pass: tone mapping is a fixed property of the backend, and on macOS Filament applies the sRGB transfer function in its post-processing pass. Missing: any effect that content or the host can declare, select or control; the architecture document says custom post-processing effects of other engines do not transfer.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
capability: Level of detail and streaming order
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what to send first, a large scene still arrives, it just pops and stalls on the way in.
note: A distance gate loads deeper levels of a map-managed scene as the camera nears, which chooses what to send first by proximity. Missing: no authored detail levels, no screen-coverage selection among alternatives, and loaded nodes are never released; the architecture document says it does not yet specify how content carries detail levels.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Only content captured as splats is affected: a system that cannot draw them shows nothing of it, while mesh content is untouched.
note: Searched the public RP1 repositories at their main heads on 2026-10-20 - Sneeze (986fc4c), Rubidium (3b8a68e), SneezeDoc (8e26da5), SneezeSDK (44d0346), RMAP (0fd7efb) and Map (0e6d26a), all text files including source and the architecture document, for splat, Gaussian, radiance field and 3DGS on 2026-10-20; the only hits are the letters inside a platform-name string and a SIMD splat instruction in a vendored decoder. The model loader lists the glTF extensions it enables and none is a splat extension, and the architecture document says everything the browser displays arrives as glTF.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: The same holds for point clouds and volumetric video, which travel in forms few systems read.
note: Searched the public RP1 repositories at their main heads on 2026-10-20 - Sneeze (986fc4c), Rubidium (3b8a68e), SneezeDoc (8e26da5), SneezeSDK (44d0346), RMAP (0fd7efb) and Map (0e6d26a), all text files including source and the architecture document, for point cloud, voxel, volumetric video and volume on 2026-10-20; the model loader maps only triangle primitives and skips points, and no code builds an ANARI volume. The architecture document lists volumes among the objects ANARI describes, so the area is in scope but not built.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Labels, signs and name tags lose their font and layout when the two systems disagree, so the text degrades while the rest of the asset is fine.
note: Legible text is drawn through RmlUi, an internal engine dependency rather than a named extension: RML and CSS documents, with FreeType fonts, are rasterized into pixel buffers and drawn as quads in the scene, and panels are a core node class reachable from guest code. Missing: fonts cannot be carried or referenced by the fabric because they are host-owned, and the panel is display-only because pointer and keyboard input are not wired.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Authored viewpoints are part of a scene, and losing them costs the arrival shot, not the scene.
note: The manifest's Primary block carries one authored camera position and rotation for the default view, and the per-scene flattening also frames the scene for that camera. There is no viewpoint list and no way to move between named viewpoints, and the camera get and set methods reserved in the published interface are marked not implemented, so guest content cannot move the view either.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: If the receiving system cannot rebuild the same tree, parenting and transforms collapse and the asset does not assemble at all.
note: The scene begins at Data.Scene and nests through aChildren arrays; parentage comes from tree position. Each node is a fixed wire record with blocks for head, name, type, owner, resource, transform, orbit, bound and properties. Node handles are per publisher identity rather than scene wide, so the same fabric loaded twice into one container shares one namespace.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A disagreement about handedness or axis order puts every object in the wrong place or mirrored, which is the classic hand fix.
note: Position, rotation and scale are three, four and three 64-bit floats at fixed offsets in a 528-byte record, and every node composes a full translate-rotate-scale and inherits its parent's, with no class exception. That precision is unusually good. But no handedness and no up axis is declared anywhere in the wire record or the published interface header: the shipped corpus is Z-up purely by convention. The local row records an observed integration failure that no public file states: mounting one of these fabrics into a Y-up host laid the scene on its side with no error, so the integration had to make an up-axis declaration required with no default.
sources: https://github.com/MetaversalCorp/SneezeSDK/blob/main/include/sneeze_abi.h | https://github.com/MetaversalCorp/Sneeze/blob/main/src/sneeze/control/Control.md | Open Spatial Lab wow-spec, SpatialFabricSubtree upAxis (observed integration requirement, no public source states it)

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: The file is the boundary: if the second system cannot open it, nothing else on this list matters.
note: The fabric file is the container: a compact JSON Web Signature whose payload holds the serialized manifest under a data claim, with members for container name, declared services and a module list of url and hash pairs, and the scene tree under Data.Scene. The public sample fabric in the engine repository is exactly that, and the browser signs and verifies these files from its own command line.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A mesh encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a mesh, and the compression choice is where this usually breaks.
note: The format encodes no meshes itself. A node names an external resource by reference and the engine decides what it is by content, parsing a binary or JSON glTF into a render model and treating anything else as an image texture; the tutorial fabrics resolve those references to glTF binary files. Geometry is therefore delegated to a registered format and only the reference is standardised. Two of the vendor's own public notes disagree about what is then drawn: the scene note says the built model is read from the node, while the compositor note says glTF binaries are not parsed there and physical nodes render as boxes for now.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Device-specific texture compression is the common failure: the model arrives untextured and someone must re-export it.
note: Embedded PNG and JPEG images are decoded to 8-bit RGBA, with larger maps reduced to 1024 pixels on a side. Compressed GPU formats such as KTX2 and WebP parse but are not decoded, so those maps stay empty, although the architecture document names KTX as the intended companion format.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Carrying materials without loss is what "renders in another system" means, and only two subjects reach this row natively today.
note: Materials travel as glTF metallic-roughness definitions plus a few extensions, and VRM MToon materials are reduced to a dielectric with a shade colour, so a toon look is approximated rather than carried. No neutral material interchange such as MaterialX is read; the architecture document mentions it only as an authoring tool that compiles down.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A clip that cannot be read leaves the object still, and an avatar that cannot move is not an avatar.
note: Node translation, rotation and scale clips with step, linear and cubic-spline interpolation are loaded from glTF and replayed, looping clip 0 of the attached model. Morph-weight channels are skipped, and only the first clip plays by default.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: The bone hierarchy is what makes a body move correctly elsewhere; without an agreed one, motion has nothing to bind to.
note: The loader records glTF skins as joint node lists with inverse-bind matrices and the renderer applies them as per-instance bone palettes with GPU skinning, so a rigged body deforms as authored. Reading only: nothing writes a rig back out.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Blend shapes carry facial detail, so losing them freezes a face rather than stopping the transfer.
note: Searched the public RP1 repositories at their main heads on 2026-10-20 - Sneeze (986fc4c), Rubidium (3b8a68e), SneezeDoc (8e26da5), SneezeSDK (44d0346), RMAP (0fd7efb) and Map (0e6d26a), all text files including source and the architecture document, for morph, blend shape and morph target on 2026-10-20; the only hits are note that morph-weight channels are skipped on load. The architecture document lists morph targets among what glTF carries, so the area is in scope.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A scene without agreed instancing still loads, it just costs far more memory and frames.
note: Copies are implicit by URL: nodes that load the same URL share one cached download and one cached CPU model, and the ANARI backend shares mesh geometry with a per-node instance. There is no declared instancing mechanism in the fabric and no glTF instancing extension is enabled.

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: Layered references are a working convenience, and flattening on export is the fallback that keeps the asset moving.
note: Nested fabrics compose recursively. A node marked as an attachment point starts a fetch of the child fabric, and the parent's scene code parses that child and verifies its signature and chain on its own, so a trusted parent confers nothing on an unverified child. The composition is transclusion, not travel: the child is drawn in the parent's accumulated frame. The local row records an observed property no public file states: cycles and fan-out were proven bounded in this project's working reader.
sources: https://github.com/MetaversalCorp/Sneeze/blob/main/src/context/scene/Scene.md | MSF observed-format note, section 8 (observed bound on cycles and fan-out)

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A metre read as a centimetre makes the asset useless on arrival, and rescaling by hand is the fix the use case forbids.
note: The wire record declares no units. The engine has since dropped its astronomical-unit path and accumulates all geometry in metres, which removes one trap, but it still gives each scene one flattening factor computed from that scene's own reach, so authored size is not what reaches the screen and a nested child inherits the parent's factor rather than getting its own. The only way to gain precision inside a body is to make that fabric the root. The local row records an observed composition failure that no public file states: a fabric whose native unit was the astronomical unit read as one metre when composed into a one-to-one room, so the integration had to make a units-per-metre value required with no default.
sources: https://github.com/MetaversalCorp/Sneeze/blob/main/src/sneeze/control/Control.md | Open Spatial Lab design note, precision domain (observed composition failure, no public source states it)

subject: RP1 Spatial Fabric
interop_reason: A signed record of who made an asset lets a receiver trust it; without one the asset still works but nobody can check its history.
note: The signature answers who published these bytes: RS256 over an X.509 chain carried in the JWS header, and the publisher's durable identity is the SHA-256 of the leaf certificate's public key, so it survives certificate renewal. Two cautions, both from the vendor's own public material. The sample fabric shipped in the engine repository is signed by a test certificate authority, not public infrastructure.
