subject: Open AR Cloud (Open Spatial Computing Platform)
interop_reason: A roster that does not cross operators means you cannot see who is where, but you can still be there.
note: Services and content have presence; people do not. A node announces itself with coverage and a lifetime, must dispose that announcement when it leaves gracefully, and service records are synchronised peer to peer across country-level providers, so a client can learn what is live in an area across operators. There is no roster of participants: the word roster does not occur, and the reference client shares participant poses over message queue topics named in a deployment's own configuration rather than by any specified protocol.

subject: Open AR Cloud (Open Spatial Computing Platform)
interop_reason: A destination name that does not resolve cannot be travelled to, so naming and resolution are the first agreement.
note: This is the platform's clearest contribution and the thing the geospatial pose standard explicitly refuses to do. Every anchor, service, content bundle and tileset gets a stable address under a domain name authority, with a formal grammar, and resolution is normative and ordered: validate, cache, advertised resolver, then a required web fallback at a well-known path that every authority must serve. Authorities are even told to keep redirects alive for a year after a handover.

subject: Open AR Cloud (Open Spatial Computing Platform)
interop_reason: Worlds can be reached by a known address, so discovery adds reach rather than making it possible.
note: Finding things without knowing them in advance is the platform's founding purpose, and it is answered twice over. The original services keep a spatial registry of service providers and of content, described by their own authors as a name service with spatial context. SpatialDDS adds a two-layer model: a bootstrap that finds the bus by local name service, a geographic name service binding, a printed code or a beacon, and a spatial search that returns service manifests over the web without joining the bus. One caution: the association's own public timeline calls the content discovery protocol ratified in 2023, and no primary source supports that word. The repository still calls its record format a base version expected to evolve and its interface version 1.0.

subject: Open AR Cloud (Open Spatial Computing Platform)
interop_reason: A shared clock keeps events in order; without one the ordering drifts and coarse clocks still hold the session together.

note: A device interface. It covers the runtime, the session, the tracked spaces, the input actions and the frame loop, and stops there. Nothing in the core specification or in any ratified extension touches this.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Content pinned to the Earth must land in the same place in the other system, and a pose that cannot be read puts it somewhere else.
note: Only through XR_ANDROID_geospatial, a Google extension that is not ratified. It reports latitude, longitude and altitude with an orientation, from a mix of motion tracking, satellite positioning and Google's visual positioning service, and it needs Google account credentials to work. Nothing ratified expresses a pose against the Earth.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A frame disagreement is measured in metres or kilometres, not in taste.
note: The same unratified single-vendor extension names one frame and only one: altitude in metres above the WGS84 ellipsoid, with a local frame of east, up and south. There is no way to declare any other reference system, and nothing ratified mentions one.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: An anchor made on one device never leaves it; the sharing case is the next row.
note: The ratified XR_EXT_spatial_anchor, one of the six spatial entity extensions, lets an application drop a point in the room and have the runtime keep correcting it as its map of the world improves. This is the strongest single piece of cross-vendor agreement in spatial computing today.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Two people in two systems must see the same thing in the same spot, and today one subject reaches this row, through an extension.
note: Half met, and the missing half is in the specification rather than in implementations. Persistence across sessions is ratified: XR_EXT_spatial_persistence and XR_EXT_spatial_persistence_operations give an anchor a stable identifier that survives a reboot. Sharing is absent. The persistence store has exactly two scopes, one read-only and system managed, the other bounded to the same device, the same user and the same application, and the anchor extension defers sharing to other extensions that do not exist in ratified form. Every extension in the registry with sharing in its name is single-vendor and unratified: XR_FB_spatial_entity_sharing, XR_META_spatial_entity_sharing, XR_META_spatial_entity_group_sharing, XR_BD_spatial_anchor_sharing and XR_ANDROID_anchor_sharing_export. Godot's documentation says sharing is not supported in the spatial entities specification, and that claim holds.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Recovering pose from imagery can fall back to satellite position and manual alignment, at worse accuracy.
note: Only inside XR_ANDROID_geospatial, which is single-vendor and unratified, and which recovers pose by matching the camera against street imagery. There is no ratified way to ask a runtime for a camera-derived pose, and no way to ask a different provider for one.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: City-scale data is streamed by tile, and a tileset the receiving client cannot stream has to be converted before it is usable.
note: A device interface. It covers the runtime, the session, the tracked spaces, the input actions and the frame loop, and stops there. Nothing in the core specification or in any ratified extension touches this.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A structured description of an interior makes placement and routing better; without one both are cruder, and nothing reaches this row today.
note: The ratified XR_EXT_spatial_plane_tracking finds the flat surfaces of a room and labels them wall, floor, ceiling, table or uncategorised, and XR_EXT_spatial_marker_tracking reads printed codes fixed to a place. That is a live read-out of one room, not a structured description: no rooms, no doors, no connectivity and nothing that can be written down and handed to another system.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: The visitor's app and the device runtime are two independent systems, and if they cannot start an immersive session the visit does not happen.
note: This is the centre of the specification. A session has nine declared states and the runtime drives the application through them by event, from idle through ready, synchronised, visible and focused to stopping and exiting, with the frame loop running in between.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A world that reads controllers differently is harder to use, and pointer and text paths remain.
note: Controllers are reached through actions rather than buttons. The application declares what it wants to know, suggests bindings for known interaction profiles, and the runtime decides which physical control answers. That indirection is what lets one application work across hardware it has never heard of, and it is the part of the design most worth copying.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Hand tracking adds a way in, and its absence falls back to controllers.
note: XR_EXT_hand_tracking is ratified and multi-vendor, and returns a fixed set of 26 named joints per hand. A companion ratified extension, XR_EXT_hand_tracking_data_source, says whether the pose came from real hands or from a controller. Hand meshes and gestures remain single-vendor and unratified.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Gaze is an aid with privacy limits, and everything works without it.
note: XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction is ratified and multi-vendor, with contributors from Tobii, Microsoft, Oculus, Varjo and Magic Leap. It exposes gaze as a pose the action system can bind to, which keeps the raw signal behind the same permission machinery as any other input.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Touch feedback is felt when it is missing, and nothing stops.
note: Touch feedback is a core output action, sent through the same action system as input. Richer waveform feedback exists only in unratified extensions: XR_FB_haptic_amplitude_envelope and XR_FB_haptic_pcm from Meta, and XR_EXT_haptic_parametric, which despite its multi-vendor tag is not ratified.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A world that cannot ask what the arriving device can do will guess, and guessing wrong costs quality rather than entry.
note: Discovery is layered and mandatory: the application enumerates the extensions the runtime offers before creating an instance, asks the system for its properties, and enumerates view configurations and blend modes. Nothing optional can be used without first being found.

subject: OpenXR

subject: OpenXR

subject: OpenXR

subject: OpenXR

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Actions that arrive without their embodiment, frame and units cannot be replayed elsewhere, so an agent acts only in the system it was written for.
note: OpenXR is a device interface covering the runtime, the session, tracked spaces, input actions and the frame loop, and it carries no agent's actions in or out as time-sampled data with an embodiment, a frame and units.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A panorama whose projection is not stated is still an image, but the receiver has to guess before it can use it as a backdrop or as a light.
note: OpenXR is a device interface covering the runtime, the session, tracked spaces, input actions and the frame loop, and it carries no full 360-degree view of a place as an image with its projection stated.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A reconstruction that cannot leave the device that made it keeps the room private to one session, so anything placed against it has to be fitted again elsewhere.
note: Core OpenXR has no reading of the room at all. The ratified spatial plane tracking extension, built on the spatial entity framework, is the cross-vendor way to get planes with their bounds, polygon and a 2D mesh. A full environment mesh is vendor-only and unratified: Google's scene meshing extension, Meta's room mesh, and Microsoft's older scene understanding, which the specification now marks obsolete.

subject: OpenXR
capability: Semantic labelling of the real world
interop_reason: Labels each vendor names differently still serve one application, but a second one cannot act on floor or sky without being rewritten for that vendor.
note: Plane semantic labels are ratified and cross-vendor, with a short list — uncategorised, floor, wall, ceiling and table. Richer labelling is vendor-specific and unratified: Meta's spatial entity semantic label extension adds door and window frames and inner and invisible wall faces. There is no per-pixel class channel anywhere in the registry.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Depth reported in units the receiver does not share puts real surfaces at the wrong distance, so content is placed badly rather than not at all.
note: Environment depth reaches the application only through Meta's unratified extension, which hands over depth maps of the real world around the headset in a swapchain, with an option for the runtime to remove the hands. No ratified extension and no part of the core specification carries a depth map of the room.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Whether real surfaces hide virtual content is drawn on the device that sees them, and none of that decision crosses to a second system.
note: Occlusion against the real world is a compositor feature of one vendor. Varjo's environment depth estimation lets the compositor mix real and virtual content by depth so that layers submitted with depth are occluded correctly. It is not ratified, and core OpenXR composites layers in submission order with no knowledge of where real surfaces are.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: How much of the real room a runtime lets through is its own presentation, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.
note: The core has the coarse control and nothing finer. An application asks which environment blend modes the system supports and then picks one — opaque, additive or alpha blend — on every frame, which is how much of the room shows through at all. Cutting a hole in a virtual environment, styling the passthrough image or placing it as its own layer needs vendor extensions, and not one of them is in the ratified set.

subject: OpenXR
capability: Face and body tracking as input
interop_reason: A face and body stream in a shape the receiver does not read leaves the avatar still rather than absent, and its privacy terms have to be agreed with it.
note: Nothing in the specification with all ratified extensions tracks a face or a body: searching the ratified text for face tracking returns no result. The face and body tracking extensions in the registry are single-vendor and unratified, so a portable application cannot count on them, and eye gaze — the one ratified piece of the person's own state — is an interaction path, not an expression stream.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A place that arrives without its walkable surface and arrival points still loads, but whoever opens it has to work out where a body may stand and where a portal lands.
note: The specification introduces OpenXR as the interface between an XR application and a runtime for virtual, augmented and mixed reality. OpenXR hands an application tracked spaces, views and input. It carries no scene, so there is no place description in which a walkable surface or an arrival point could travel.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A published unit of logic whose name resolves to something else elsewhere still runs, but nobody can be sure which code they called.
note: The specification introduces OpenXR as the interface between an XR application and a runtime for virtual, augmented and mixed reality. OpenXR runs no code on anyone's behalf and publishes no units of logic. Its own extension names are registered with Khronos, which is a naming rule for the API, not an address for world logic.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A receiving world that cannot tell what review arriving content has already had still shows it, and has to repeat the whole review itself.
note: The specification introduces OpenXR as the interface between an XR application and a runtime for virtual, augmented and mixed reality. A device runtime interface has no publishing path: no content passes through OpenXR on its way to an audience, so no review can stand in that path.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Two maps of one place with no published transform between them put the same content in two positions, so a person arrives beside where they meant to be.
note: The ratified spatial entity extensions give an application anchors, planes, markers and persistence keyed by a UUID that survives between sessions, which is as close as OpenXR comes. There is still no map object with a version and a lifecycle, and no transform published between two maps of the same place, so two devices cannot be told they are in the same map.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A service that never declares where it applies still answers, so a client has to call it and find out instead of testing whether it is relevant.
note: Only through the single-vendor XR_ANDROID_geospatial extension, which is not ratified: an application can ask whether Google's visual positioning service is available at a given latitude and longitude, and use the answer to decide whether to create a geospatial tracker. The area is queried rather than published: the specification gives no boundary or dataset declaration a client can hold and test offline, and nothing ratified speaks about geography at all.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A receiver must distinguish required additions from optional ones or it cannot safely interpret an arriving asset or exchange.
note: OpenXR instance creation names enabled extensions and rejects unsupported requested extensions; structure chains and extension-specific commands carry their additions.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Named subsets make compatible requirements easier to select, while systems can still agree on the individual requirements without a named profile.
note: An application declares the API version it needs and an instance names its extensions, and a runtime that cannot meet the version must refuse, so a version level (1.0 or 1.1) is a stated contract. There are no named subsets smaller than a version, such as a bundle of extensions an implementation and content could both declare.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Content still arrives when color conventions differ, but its colors and brightness can change visibly.
note: The named XR_FB_color_space extension enumerates color spaces and selects the application's submitted color interpretation; supported spaces remain runtime-dependent.

note: OpenXR carries no scene or asset, so it has nowhere to attach descriptive properties to a scene or its parts. The only asset-level data is runtime identifiers such as a render model cache identifier and node names, which are not declared descriptive metadata.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: A scene or visit can continue when interface layouts differ, but carried controls and information may become hard to use.
note: Core quad layers give two-dimensional regions their size and scene-relative pose; child-widget layout and alignment semantics remain application-defined.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Estimating illumination for the local view stays within the sensing and rendering system and requires no agreement between the independent worlds in the four use cases.
note: XR_ANDROID_light_estimation exposes runtime ambient and directional illumination estimates; this is registered extension support, not an OpenXR core requirement.

interop_reason: Shared marker references improve physical alignment across systems, while a scene or visit can still proceed with another placement method.
note: XR_EXT_spatial_marker_tracking defines marker-specific spatial capabilities and tracked poses; marker formats and support are explicitly advertised by the runtime.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: An asset with external resources cannot load intact if the receiver cannot resolve its resource references in the intended context.

subject: OpenXR
capability: Pose series and live pose streams
interop_reason: Systems exchanging moving subjects must agree on the time and frame of each pose or the subject's movement cannot be reconstructed correctly.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Receiving text through a local input field or keyboard interface is a device-side interaction and need not be shared between worlds.
note: XR_META_virtual_keyboard supplies committed UTF-8 text and separate keyboard events through a named optional runtime extension.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: The choice of image layers sent to a device compositor is local presentation work and need not be shared across a world boundary.
note: Core projection and quad composition layers define image submissions, poses, sizes and blending flags; additional layer shapes require their named extensions.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Shared bounds let a receiver select content before loading its geometry; without them the content can still move but loads and traverses less efficiently.
note: The ratified XR_EXT_spatial_entity gives each sensed spatial entity an optional 3D bounds component as an oriented box. It describes real-world entities the runtime finds, not authored scene content, and there is no spatial index or traversal structure.

subject: OpenXR
interop_reason: Losing agreed object sets weakens grouped scene operations while the individual objects can still be transferred and rendered.

interop_reason: A moved object or avatar can still load when constraints are lost, but linked movement and pose behavior degrade.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: This row is the portal itself, and the travel use case is nothing but the handoff.
note: Searched the SpatialDDS 1.8 full specification, its section files, IDL and example manifests (commit 84220cf) for handoff, hand-off, handover, migrate and transfer on 2026-10-20; only TaskHandoff (an informative example in which one agent passes a task to another) and writer-ownership transfer for a keyed instance (Appendix M.2) matched. Neither moves session or user state from one deployment to another; a client arriving elsewhere bootstraps again.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A roster that does not cross operators means you cannot see who is where, but you can still be there.
note: Participants publish an announcement with capabilities, topics and coverage, a graceful departure message, a time-to-live backstop for silent loss, and defined re-announce rates, so which services are present and what they cover is observable across operators. This is presence of services only: the service kind list has no agent or person member, and Future Directions proposes an agent kind for 1.9, so presence of people or agents is not part of discovery.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A destination name that does not resolve cannot be travelled to, so naming and resolution are the first agreement.
note: A spatialdds:// URI names an authority, zone, type and identifier, a formal grammar is given, and a fixed resolution order turns the name into a manifest. Topic names follow a defined pattern with a version segment.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Worlds can be reached by a known address, so discovery adds reach rather than making it possible.
note: Discovery works in two layers: network bootstrap (mDNS, geospatial DNS, a well-known HTTPS path, QR codes) and service discovery by coverage, through an HTTP search endpoint or announcements and queries on the bus.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A shared clock keeps events in order; without one the ordering drifts and coarse clocks still hold the session together.
note: Time values are UTC seconds on the POSIX count, producers declare clock source and accuracy in metadata, and consumers must compensate clock offsets before associating data across sources. Clock synchronisation itself is left to PTP, NTP or GNSS, and events from different writers are merged by a consumer-chosen window.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: With no shared base identifier the same person or agent is a stranger in every world they enter.
note: Writers, agents, frames and entities each carry a stable identifier (a source identifier, a frame UUID, a minted entity UUID), and URIs name an authority. Nothing binds an identifier to a verifiable controller, and rotating source identifiers are recommended for privacy.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Claims about age, membership or ownership are worthless if the receiving world cannot read them.
note: Credentials are not defined by the specification. It requires DDS Security with public-key authentication for on-bus access and allows OAuth 2.0 and mutual TLS to be named in the authentication hint for HTTP resources.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A credential nobody can ask for or present is not a credential, and one subject reaches this row natively today.
note: Presentation is left to the delegated mechanisms: bearer tokens go in the standard Authorization header for HTTP resolution and DDS Security performs its own handshake on the bus. The specification defines no request-and-present exchange of its own.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A world that cannot read what an arriving person or agent is allowed to do must either refuse it or trust it blindly.
note: On the bus, access is governed by DDS Security permissions documents, and the authentication hint can carry an OAuth scope such as vps.localize. The specification does not define its own capability or permission token that a third party can read.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Without selective disclosure the traveller over-shares, which is a harm rather than a stop.
note: Privacy mitigations for pose streams are given as guidance (SHOULD): coarser pose precision, truncated history, rotating source identifiers and purpose limitation. Disclosure control is by operator policy, with no selective-disclosure mechanism.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Relationships and standing that do not travel leave the person present but unknown.
note: Portable relationships and standing are social-graph features; SpatialDDS describes physical-world observations and defines no relationship between people. The Open World Model leaves even entity-to-entity relationships as reserved open design.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Content pinned to the Earth must land in the same place in the other system, and a pose that cannot be read puts it somewhere else.
note: GeoPose carries latitude, longitude and ellipsoidal height in WGS84 with a quaternion in the local east-north-up frame, in the same component order as OGC GeoPose, and a covariance. FramedPose carries a local metric pose in a named frame.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A frame disagreement is measured in metres or kilometres, not in taste.
note: Every pose names its frame with a FrameRef (UUID, readable name, axis convention and scale), frames form an acyclic graph, earth-fixed roots encode WGS84, and coverage elements may name an EPSG code. Local frames must be tied back to an earth-fixed root by anchors or manifests.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: An anchor made on one device never leaves it; the sharing case is the next row.
note: Poses and frames can be local, and datasets without satellite positioning are supported, but the only anchor type is a geo-anchor that requires a global pose. A device-local anchor can only be expressed as a named local frame.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Two people in two systems must see the same thing in the same spot, and today one subject reaches this row, through an extension.
note: The Core profile defines a geo-anchored reference point with pose, method, confidence and covariance, and the Anchors profile adds anchor sets, incremental updates and a registry so devices share the same anchors across sessions. An anchor can name the content manifest attached to it.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Recovering pose from imagery can fall back to satellite position and manual alignment, at worse accuracy.
note: The AR+Geo extension (spatial.argeo) defines a localisation request and response, correlated by query identifier, with query imagery or descriptors passed by blob reference and quality requirements and a status in the reply. Appendix L adds calibration tests for the claimed accuracy.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: City-scale data is streamed by tile, and a tileset the receiving client cannot stream has to be converted before it is usable.
note: Core defines tile keys by grid position and level, tile metadata with a bounding box and encoding name, patches and blob transport, and a tileset manifest. The tiling scheme is only a generic quadtree or 3D grid, with no mapping to a geospatial tile hierarchy and no refinement rules, so interoperability depends on the encoding named.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A structured description of an interior makes placement and routing better; without one both are cruder, and nothing reaches this row today.
note: Vertical extent can be stated with a 3D bounding box and a pose can carry frames at building, floor and room level, but no interior model is defined. The specification tells composed deployments to refer to CityGML or IndoorGML identifiers rather than restate a building hierarchy.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The visitor's app and the device runtime are two independent systems, and if they cannot start an immersive session the visit does not happen.
note: Starting and ending an immersive session on a device is a runtime function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices. Its 'session' notions are DDS domain membership and bootstrap, not an immersive session.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A world that reads controllers differently is harder to use, and pointer and text paths remain.
note: Handheld controller buttons, sticks and pose are device input; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Hand tracking adds a way in, and its absence falls back to controllers.
note: Articulated hand pose as an input source is device input; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices. Its only body keypoints describe people detected by perception.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Gaze is an aid with privacy limits, and everything works without it.
note: Gaze as an input source is device input; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Touch feedback is felt when it is missing, and nothing stops.
note: Touch feedback to a user is an output device function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A world that cannot ask what the arriving device can do will guess, and guessing wrong costs quality rather than entry.
note: Devices and services advertise what they provide through capability blocks (supported profiles and feature flags) and typed sensor metadata, and consumers can negotiate a region of interest with a sensor. This covers sensing capability only, not display, input or compute capability of a client.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The language a world writes its rules in is its own business and never has to cross.
note: The language and runtime for world rules are not defined; SpatialDDS has no scripting language or runtime, and its only free-form payloads are metadata bags.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The use case says the asset must behave, so a door that will not open in the second system is the failure this row names.
note: Declarative interactivity that travels with an asset is an asset-format feature; SpatialDDS carries observations and inferred state between systems and leaves world logic to the consumers.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A host can sandbox guest content on its own; agreement only makes the limits predictable for the guest.
note: Running untrusted content safely is a runtime function; SpatialDDS exchanges typed messages and does not execute guest content.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: An agent with no agreed way to perceive and act in a world it did not come from cannot join it at all.
note: An informative Agent profile defines task requests, status, fleet availability, offers, assignments and handoffs, and Appendix H describes a model acting as a participant on the bus. It is outside the normative 1.8 text, carries task parameters as free-form JSON, and leaves allocation to applications.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Without agreed limits, guest content and agents are throttled or refused unpredictably.
note: Bounding memory, time and calls for guest content is a runtime function; SpatialDDS does not execute guest content.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: What survives a restart is mostly the host's business; it crosses the boundary only when a visitor's changes must last.
note: Latched keyed types keep their current state for late joiners and a removal rule separates retirement from silence, and anchors are durable across sessions. The specification defines no persistence service, and the Open World Model notes that latched history is held by the writer, so state does not survive a restart unless the deployment supplies it.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The use case names inventory, and items that cannot be read at the destination do not travel with the person.
note: A user's items and whether they travel are application state; SpatialDDS describes observations of the physical world and defines no inventory or item type.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The use case names preferences, and for a person who depends on comfort and accessibility settings, arriving without them ends the visit.
note: Settings and accessibility choices that follow a user are user-profile state; SpatialDDS defines no preference or profile type.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Naming content by hash makes an item the same item everywhere; without it copies drift while still loading.
note: Blobs have an identifier that may be a UUID or a content address and a SHA-256 checksum, and every asset reference carries a hash in algorithm:hex form. Content is still located by URI, and no content-addressed naming scheme is required.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A runnable experience moves between hosts far less often than an asset does, and repackaging is the fallback.
note: A content manifest describes an experience with a title, summary, tags, an availability window, a list of required SpatialDDS URIs and a list of assets with media type and hash. It lists what is needed but defines no runnable package format or entry point.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Assets reach clients over ordinary web delivery, so agreement here buys scale and cost rather than possibility.
note: Heavy content is referenced by URI with a media type and an integrity hash and fetched out of band, and discovery responses carry cache-lifetime guidance. No delivery network behaviour (mirroring, range requests, prefetch) is specified.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A reader that cannot tell which version it holds, or what to do with the parts it does not know, breaks on the first update, which is the "no hand fixes" test again.
note: Profiles carry semantic version identifiers, appendable types, a highest-compatible-minor negotiation and a published change list per release, but the compatibility promise only takes effect on formal adoption. During the 1.x series minor revisions may break the wire, and 1.8 is a draft.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Every other must row is a claim until a shared test says it holds, which is exactly what the meeting asked for.
note: Three kinds of check exist: a normative conformance suite for the web binding, normative claim-calibration tests for position-fix quality, and an informative appendix of schema-expressiveness checks against five public datasets. Wire-level interoperability between independent DDS implementations is not tested and is listed as future work.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: World generation from a prompt or an image
interop_reason: A generated place that arrives only as frames to watch still reaches the viewer, but as a recording rather than a world the receiver can open and use.
note: Generating a whole place from text or an image is a generative-model function; SpatialDDS grounds world models with real observations and predictions and does not generate scenes.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A world continued by a model still reaches a viewer, but only as what the model chooses to show, so the receiver cannot keep it or run it again.
note: The capability is the predicting model itself, which continues a world in response to the viewer; SpatialDDS says it is not an AI middleware and only carries the observations such systems consume and the predictions they produce. Appendix H.2 shows prediction results published as planned trajectories or detections, which are carried data, not the model.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: How a system turns photographs into a model is its own method, and what leaves is an ordinary asset the container and geometry rows already carry.
note: Building a textured model from photographs is a reconstruction pipeline; SpatialDDS carries the inputs and outputs of such pipelines (SLAM and structure-from-motion keyframes, features, maps) but does not define how a model is built.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so this row is what geometry encoding is for a mesh: splat content in a named format the receiving tool cannot read does not arrive at all, and re-exporting it is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: Splat scenes are carried by reference as ordinary assets with a media type and hash, and an informative note names glTF with the KHR_gaussian_splatting extension and the SPZ format. No splat payload type is defined, and the Neural profile with a GAUSSIAN_SPLAT representation tag is an informative example outside the normative text.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what arrives first, a large capture still loads, it just makes the viewer wait for the whole of it.
note: Core tiles are keyed by grid position and detail level, tile patches add, replace or remove content by revision, and a tileset manifest records the encoding and number of detail levels, so a viewer can fetch by region and level. The specification gives no rule for ordering or prioritising tiles, so progressive start-up behaviour is left to implementations.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a volumetric clip is an asset like any other: without the calibration and mask metadata a second implementation needs, what arrives is not the recording and no one can make it one by hand.
note: Tile metadata can name a volumetric encoding such as V3C or MPEG-PCC in a free-form string, and the Vision profile carries camera intrinsics, extrinsics and masks for the capture rig. No time-varying volumetric asset type or replay rule is defined, so a second implementation would need an out-of-band agreement for the encoding.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a point cloud encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a point cloud, exactly as an undecodable mesh is not a mesh, and that capture shows nothing.
note: The Lidar extension profile (spatial.sensing.lidar) defines point cloud frames with a declared cloud encoding (PCD, PLY, LAS, LAZ, raw interleaved binary, glTF with Draco, MPEG-PCC) and a point layout enumeration with fixed byte widths for the raw form.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so views that arrive without their intrinsics and extrinsics cannot be reprojected: the capture lands as loose pictures rather than as the place it recorded.
note: The Vision extension (spatial.sensing.vision) publishes a depth camera as its own stream with 16-bit millimetre depth, camera intrinsics, and a rig identifier that links it to the colour stream, with sensor extrinsics in the shared stream header. Views are separate streams rather than one multi-view object, so the grouping rests on the rig identifier.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Making an image from a viewpoint no camera occupied is a method inside one system, and what crosses to a second system is the picture it produced.
note: An informative example defines a view synthesis request (camera pose, field of view, size, requested outputs) and a response with result blobs, so an AR client can ask a mapping service for a view from a pose no camera held. It is outside the normative 1.8 text and has no registered type or topic.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a moving capture handed over as unrelated frames is not the capture: the receiver has to guess the rate and the ordering the sender already knew, and guessing is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: Sensor streams carry a stream identity, an advertised cadence, per-frame sequence numbers and timestamps, so a receiver can replay a time-varying capture at the right rate. No 4D scene representation, such as a deforming splat set or a mesh sequence with timing, is defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Whether a captured scene answers the light around it is work the receiving system does, and the asset arrives either way.
note: Making a capture respond to the lighting of its new place is a rendering and reconstruction technique; SpatialDDS defines no lighting or material model and carries captured data only.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Editing a capture after the fact
interop_reason: Editing a capture happens in the tool that holds it, and what leaves is the edited asset, which the format rows already carry.
note: Cropping, deleting or recolouring a capture is authoring-tool behaviour; SpatialDDS exchanges observations and map data and defines no editing operations.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Describing a change to a world you already made is one service's own interface, and the world that results still leaves by the ordinary export rows.
note: Editing a world by description is a generative-tool function; SpatialDDS is a data bus for observations and states that it is not AI middleware.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A generator that cannot read the specification another tool wrote still produces a world, it just will not be the world that was asked for.
note: What a generator accepts as a prompt, reference image or seed is a property of generative tools; SpatialDDS defines no generation request and is not AI middleware.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Deriving conventional assets from a generated scene
interop_reason: Derived meshes and panoramas are how a generated world reaches a conventional engine at all, and each route loses something the receiver has to be told about.
note: Converting a splat or radiance-field world into a collision mesh, panorama or video is a conversion tool function; SpatialDDS carries finished assets by reference and defines no conversion or loss statement.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Actions that arrive without their embodiment, frame and units cannot be replayed elsewhere, so an agent acts only in the system it was written for.
note: A planned trajectory carries time-stamped planned poses in a stated frame with an uncertainty estimate and a plan revision, which covers pose and camera-path actions. Joint and gripper values, embodiment and normalisation are not defined, and Appendix H.3 states that action spaces and action vectors are left to other formats.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A panorama whose projection is not stated is still an image, but the receiver has to guess before it can use it as a backdrop or as a light.
note: The Vision extension has a rig role value for an equirectangular 360-degree projection and one for a stitched panorama, so a 360-degree image can be published as a camera frame with its projection named. The specification does not define use of the image as a backdrop or light source.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A reconstruction that cannot leave the device that made it keeps the room private to one session, so anything placed against it has to be fitted again elsewhere.
note: A map descriptor can declare a mesh, occupancy grid, point cloud or voxel map kind, and tile metadata, patches and blobs carry the geometry between systems, so a device-made mesh can leave its session. Producing the mesh from device sensors and the planes or parametric room forms are not defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Semantic labelling of the real world
interop_reason: Labels each vendor names differently still serve one application, but a second one cannot act on floor or sky without being rewritten for that vendor.
note: The Semantics extension (spatial.semantics) carries 2D and 3D detections with a class label and the Vision extension carries segmentation masks (SegMask, PNG label masks). Class vocabularies are borrowed identifiers, not defined, so naming depends on a shared ontology.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Depth reported in units the receiver does not share puts real surfaces at the wrong distance, so content is placed badly rather than not at all.
note: The Vision extension (spatial.sensing.vision) defines a 16-bit depth pixel format in millimetres by default, with a declared unit override, zero meaning no measurement, and intrinsics for the depth camera.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Whether real surfaces hide virtual content is drawn on the device that sees them, and none of that decision crosses to a second system.
note: The Semantics profile is stated to serve AR occlusion, and depth frames, detections and mesh or tile maps supply the inputs. No occlusion operation or blend rule is defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: How much of the real room a runtime lets through is its own presentation, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.
note: Mixing the live camera view with rendered content is a display-runtime function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data and does not define how a renderer draws it. Camera frames appear only as sensor streams.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Face and body tracking as input
interop_reason: A face and body stream in a shape the receiver does not read leaves the avatar still rather than absent, and its privacy terms have to be agreed with it.
note: A user's own face and body pose as a live sensor stream is device input for avatars; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices. The 1.8 pose skeleton describes people observed by perception, not the user's own tracking.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A place that arrives without its walkable surface and arrival points still loads, but whoever opens it has to work out where a body may stand and where a portal lands.
note: A map descriptor can declare an occupancy-grid map kind described as for navigation planning, with the encoding named in a free-form string. Walkable surfaces, bounds and spawn points are not defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A published unit of logic whose name resolves to something else elsewhere still runs, but nobody can be sure which code they called.
note: Naming a published unit of logic permanently is not defined; SpatialDDS URIs name data resources under an authority, and the specification defines no logic units.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A receiving world that cannot tell what review arriving content has already had still shows it, and has to repeat the whole review itself.
note: Review of content before audiences see it is a platform policy function; SpatialDDS announces content and defines no review state, reviewer or review record.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Two maps of one place with no published transform between them put the same content in two positions, so a person arrives beside where they meant to be.
note: The Mapping extension (spatial.mapping) defines a map descriptor with kind, coverage, quality and lifecycle state, an inter-map alignment transform with provenance, uncertainty and evidence, and lifecycle events.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A service that never declares where it applies still answers, so a client has to call it and find out instead of testing whether it is relevant.
note: Announcements and manifests share one coverage model: a canonical frame, bounding boxes, 3D boxes, circles, geohashes, time windows and a derived-coverage list, with rules for evaluating transforms at a stated time.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A receiver must distinguish required additions from optional ones or it cannot safely interpret an arriving asset or exchange.
note: Types are declared appendable and consumers must ignore unknown appended fields and unknown top-level manifest fields. Namespaced typed key-value rows carry producer extensions, and feature flags in the capabilities block advertise optional or provisional ones.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Named subsets make compatible requirements easier to select, while systems can still agree on the individual requirements without a named profile.
note: Named profiles carry identifiers of the form spatial.<profile>/MAJOR.MINOR, a profile matrix lists each with a status, and participants advertise supported version ranges so peers can select the highest compatible minor.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Content still arrives when color conventions differ, but its colors and brightness can change visibly.
note: Camera frames declare a colour space (sRGB, Rec.709, Rec.2020 or linear) and a pixel format in the Vision extension. Output range, transfer functions beyond that list, and colour declarations for textures or rendering surfaces are not defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Domain metadata carried with an asset
interop_reason: An asset can load without shared descriptive properties, but receivers lose the classifications and facts that drive its use.
note: Namespaced typed key-value rows, with free-form JSON as a fallback, attach properties to messages, entities and manifests, and the typed-first rule keeps them readable. Key meaning is not agreed across producers, which the specification states as a bag and not a contract.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Assurance and evidence behind a claim
interop_reason: A credential can be presented without shared assurance detail, but the receiver has less evidence for deciding whether to trust it.
note: Claims about the physical world carry assurance in several forms: covariance, quality and confidence fields, a basis (observed, declared, authored or derived) on world-model entities, and calibration tests for claimed fix quality. This does not extend to how a subject's identity was established.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A receiving world cannot use a credential reliably unless it can interpret the claim vocabulary and check its structure.
note: Vocabulary and validation schemas for identity claims are outside the specification, which defines no claim format; its published JSON Schema and IDL validate manifests and bus messages, not claims about a subject.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Travel can continue with reusable identifiers, but correlating visits across relationships creates a privacy loss.
note: Guidance recommends rotating source identifiers that cannot be linked across sessions without a key held by the data controller. Pairwise identifiers per relationship and a statement of remaining correlation risk are not defined.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A moved asset remains usable without a shared preview image, but selection and arrival previews become slower or less informative.
note: Searched the SpatialDDS 1.8 full specification, its section files, IDL and example manifests (commit 84220cf) for thumbnail, preview and icon on 2026-10-20; no match. Content manifests carry a title, summary and tags but no preview image.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Travel and participation can use a shared session without encrypted subject payloads, but lack of agreement prevents confidential subject data from following safely.
note: Deployments needing confidentiality must use DDS Security cryptographic plug-ins, and services should protect location and sensor payloads beyond a trusted network. Recipient key material and algorithms are left to DDS Security and are not identified in SpatialDDS messages.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: After identity keys change, a destination must find the applicable verification material to recognize the same person or agent safely.
note: Searched the SpatialDDS 1.8 full specification, its section files, IDL and example manifests (commit 84220cf) for revoke, revocation, rotate, renew, recovery, certificate revocation and key lifecycle on 2026-10-20; no rule matched (rotation appears only for rotating source identifiers). Key management is whatever the DDS Security deployment provides.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A destination cannot rely on an issued credential for admission or authority unless the agreed mechanism lets it discover that the credential has been withdrawn.
note: Searched the SpatialDDS 1.8 full specification, its section files, IDL and example manifests (commit 84220cf) for revoke, revocation, suspend, status list, certificate revocation list and online status check on 2026-10-20; no credential status mechanism matched. Withdrawal appears only for content and topics, not for credentials.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: A scene or visit can continue when interface layouts differ, but carried controls and information may become hard to use.
note: Layout of two-dimensional interface regions is a UI-toolkit matter; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data and does not define how a renderer draws it.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Estimating illumination for the local view stays within the sensing and rendering system and requires no agreement between the independent worlds in the four use cases.
note: Runtime estimates of environmental illumination are an AR-runtime output; SpatialDDS sensing profiles cover radar, lidar, vision, inertial and radio data and define no light estimate.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Shared marker references improve physical alignment across systems, while a scene or visit can still proceed with another placement method.
note: Searched the SpatialDDS 1.8 full specification, its section files, IDL and example manifests (commit 84220cf) for marker, fiducial, ArUco, AprilTag and image target on 2026-10-20; the only matches are QR codes as a bootstrap discovery channel and the end-of-replay marker in the web binding. A scanned landmark can be published as an anchor, but no marker detection or tracked-marker pose type exists.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: An asset with external resources cannot load intact if the receiver cannot resolve its resource references in the intended context.
note: A SpatialDDS URI must be resolved in a fixed order: syntax check, local cache, an advertised resolver, then a required HTTPS fallback, with defined error handling and expiry rules for authorities.

subject: SpatialDDS
capability: Pose series and live pose streams
interop_reason: Systems exchanging moving subjects must agree on the time and frame of each pose or the subject's movement cannot be reconstructed correctly.
note: A planned trajectory carries time-stamped waypoints with velocity and uncertainty and a revision rule, and live pose streams carry timestamps and sequence numbers. No interpolation or sampling rule is declared, so how to read between two poses is left to the consumer.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Turning local pointing input into a scene hit stays inside the receiving application and does not require agreement between independent worlds.
note: Turning a ray or touch into a picked object is a runtime and application function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: Receiving text through a local input field or keyboard interface is a device-side interaction and need not be shared between worlds.
note: Receiving typed text from a person is a device-input function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data between systems and defines no interface to a person's input devices.

subject: SpatialDDS
interop_reason: The choice of image layers sent to a device compositor is local presentation work and need not be shared across a world boundary.
note: Submitting image layers to a display compositor is a display-runtime function; SpatialDDS exchanges spatial data and does not define how a renderer draws it.

subject: SpatialDDS

subject: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC)

subject: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC)
interop_reason: Credentials still verify without a shared registry, but each receiver must decide alone whom to trust, so acceptance differs from world to world.
note: STAC describes data files and has no people, credentials or claims about them, so governed trust registries is outside its purpose.

subject: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC)
