subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: An asset that arrives against a different surface model still loads, but the further apart the two models are the more the look drifts.
note: The shape component gives three lighting models for a surface: a Phong material, a physically based material (with metallic and roughness terms) and an unlit material, with texture bindings for each and an alpha mode, plus shader nodes for anything beyond them. The physically based node was aligned with the common asset format's material.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A moved scene whose lights are read differently is lit wrong rather than lost.
note: A dedicated clause gives the lighting equations and the shadow requirements, so the standard says how a lit surface should look rather than leaving it to each reader.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Effects applied after the main pass are the receiving system's taste and carry nothing across.
note: Fog blends the colour of every object toward a fog colour by distance from the camera, which is blending of object colours and not a stage applied after the main render pass, so no part of the definition is met. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, 57 clause, profile and front-matter pages, for post-process, bloom, tone map, blur, depth of field, screen space and after render on 2026-10-20; the only tone-map hits are ToneMappedVolumeStyle, a volume rendering style, and the only blur hit is MotionBlur, an optional browser-option flag (Boolean, default false) with no post-pass stage defined.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Level of detail and streaming order
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what to send first, a large scene still arrives, it just pops and stalls on the way in.
note: A level-of-detail node switches representations by distance, and the geospatial clause adds a terrain form of it that also loads and unloads children.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Only content captured as splats is affected: a system that cannot draw them shows nothing of it, while mesh content is untouched.
note: Captured data can be drawn as point sets or as volume data, but there is no splat primitive and no radiance-field representation or rendering rule. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for splat, Gaussian, radiance field, NeRF and neural on 2026-10-20; no match.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The same holds for point clouds and volumetric video, which travel in forms few systems read.
note: Clause 41 covers rendering volumetric data sets inside a scene, which no other subject on the asset side of this map has in a ratified form.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Labels, signs and name tags lose their font and layout when the two systems disagree, so the text degrades while the rest of the asset is fine.
note: A text node with a font style node covering family, style, direction, justification and language. Text is turned into geometry, so it is legible in three dimensions rather than pasted on as an image.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Authored viewpoints are part of a scene, and losing them costs the arrival shot, not the scene.
note: Named viewpoints in perspective or orthographic form, only one bound at a time, plus a navigation information node that says how the user may move. Viewpoints are addressable, which is what makes deep links into a scene possible.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: If the receiving system cannot rebuild the same tree, parenting and transforms collapse and the asset does not assemble at all.
note: Clause 4 defines the scene graph, the transformation hierarchy and the rules for ancestors and descendants, including that a node may not be its own ancestor.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A disagreement about handedness or axis order puts every object in the wrong place or mirrored, which is the classic hand fix.
note: One fixed convention, right-handed with the vertical axis up, stated in the concepts clause. It matches the common asset format, which makes exchange between them straightforward.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The file is the boundary: if the second system cannot open it, nothing else on this list matters.
note: The architecture part defines the scene contents; the byte-level encodings that carry them sit in a companion part of the same standard, not in this document. Cite the encodings separately if the question is about file bytes.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A mesh encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a mesh, and the compression choice is where this usually breaks.
note: Three separate clauses cover rendering primitives, three-dimensional geometry and two-dimensional geometry, with a further clause for engineering geometry.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Device-specific texture compression is the common failure: the model arrives untextured and someone must re-export it.
note: A texturing clause plus separate clauses for three-dimensional textures, cube maps and texture projection.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Carrying materials without loss is what "renders in another system" means, and only two subjects reach this row natively today.
note: The physically based material node was deliberately aligned with the common asset format's material, and the standard says so in a note. This is the clearest worked example on the whole map of two standards bodies making an exchange lossless on purpose.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A clip that cannot be read leaves the object still, and an avatar that cannot move is not an avatar.
note: Animation is expressed as interpolator nodes driven by a time sensor and wired to targets by routes, rather than as a clip. That makes it flexible inside the file and awkward to lift out as a portable clip.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The bone hierarchy is what makes a body move correctly elsewhere; without an agreed one, motion has nothing to bind to.
note: The humanoid animation clause defines a joint, a segment and an attachment site, giving a bone hierarchy with defined semantics rather than an anonymous tree.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Blend shapes carry facial detail, so losing them freezes a face rather than stopping the transfer.
note: The displacer node moves a named set of vertices by a list of offsets, which is a blend shape by another name, and is how facial detail is carried.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A scene without agreed instancing still loads, it just costs far more memory and frames.
note: A reused node is inserted again as the same node rather than copied, giving it several parents, so one definition can appear many times, each time under its own transform; the rendering component says geometry property nodes are separate so they can be shared. There is no separate node that repeats a mesh from a list of transforms.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Layered references are a working convenience, and flattening on export is the fallback that keeps the asset moving.
note: A scene can pull in another file, and named values can be imported and exported across that boundary; prototypes let a definition live in a separate file. What is missing is override: there is no way for one source to change a value inside another, and no layering with a strength order. That is the gap the scene description standard was built to fill.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A metre read as a centimetre makes the asset useless on arrival, and rescaling by hand is the fix the use case forbids.
note: Metres by default, with base units for angle, force, mass and time each tied to an international units standard. Unlike the common asset format, a file may declare a different length unit, so a reader must honour the declaration rather than assume metres.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: An item that arrives with no readable terms cannot be lawfully worn, shown or sold, so the move fails at the rights boundary even when every byte arrives.
note: The world information node carries a free-text field that the standard says may hold author information, copyright and usage instructions, the geospatial metadata node has a copyright field, and a file header can hold name and value metadata. Missing: any structured licence terms, so a recipient cannot tell from the file what it may do with the asset except by reading the text.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A signed record of who made an asset lets a receiver trust it; without one the asset still works but nobody can check its history.
note: Part 1 defines no signed record of who made an asset. The companion compressed binary encoding optionally applies XML signature to scene fragments, which can show who signed and that the content is unchanged, but it holds no record of how the asset was made. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for signature, signed, provenance, attestation and digital on 2026-10-20; the only hits for signature were unrelated node-signature wording, so no signing is defined in Part 1.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The portable description of the body is the artefact this use case moves; with no agreement the person arrives as nothing.
note: A humanoid node gathers the joints, segments and sites into one figure, which is the portable description of a body. It does not specify clothing, wearables or expression sets.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Agreed bone names are what let animation authored anywhere play on the arriving body.
note: The humanoid clause binds a separate international standard for humanoid animation into this one, so bone names and structure are agreed rather than left to convention. This is the answer that the common asset format still lacks.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The use case names expressions, and named shapes the destination does not know leave a blank face.
note: The humanoid component has a displacer node holding named vertex offsets with a weight, and its own example is the vertices of the left eyebrow, so the mechanism for facial shape changes exists. Missing: a list of expression or viseme names in this part, so a named expression does not by itself mean the same thing in another reader; the shared vocabulary, if any, sits in the separate humanoid standard, which was not read.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Retargeting is the repair when skeletons differ, so its absence costs motion quality rather than the visit.
note: The humanoid component carries motion data per named joint and channel, and the joint names come from the shared humanoid standard, so a motion can in principle be played on another figure that uses the same joints. Missing: any rule in this part for adjusting a motion to a body of different proportions; the separate humanoid standard was not read.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Equipped items are named in the use case, and attachment points that do not survive leave items on the floor or on the wrong bone.
note: Half of this is answered, and answered by name. An HAnimSite is a grouping node whose stated second purpose is an attachment point for accessories such as jewelry and clothing; it takes children, so a hat or a strap hangs beneath it, and the humanoid node keeps a list of its sites. The names come from the humanoid animation standard that this clause binds in, so the same point means the same thing in two files from two authors, which is more than the common asset format offers. What is missing is the item. Nothing defines a wearable as a separate thing that can move from one avatar to another, there are no fitting or scaling rules for bodies of different shape, there is no ownership, and there is no way to put something on or take it off. A garment travels only inside the humanoid that already carries it.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Reduced forms matter for crowds and weak devices, and their absence costs frames, not presence.
note: The humanoid and motion nodes carry a level-of-articulation field with values from minus one to four, and the skin field accepts a level-of-detail node, so reduced figures can be expressed. Missing: the meaning of each articulation level is defined in the separate humanoid standard, not in this part, and was not read.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without a way to bind an avatar to a verifiable identity, the person who arrives cannot be shown to be the person who left.
note: The humanoid node carries a free-text information field meant for author and copyright details, which nothing verifies or binds to a credential. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for credential, identity, verifiable, authentication, certificate, account and owner on 2026-10-20; no binding of an avatar to an identity or credential found.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Mass and velocity carried across make a moved object behave nearly the same; their absence changes the behaviour without stopping it.
note: Clause 37 defines rigid bodies and rigid body collections. It is in the fullest profile, so a reader may conform to the standard without implementing it.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Collision shapes travel separately from visible geometry, and losing them means objects pass through each other until the destination builds its own.
note: Collidable shapes and offsets, collision spaces, collision collections, a collision sensor and a contact node, kept separate from the visible geometry.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Hinges and sliders that do not survive turn an assembly into loose parts, which is a loss of behaviour rather than of the asset.
note: Six joint types: ball, single-axis hinge, double-axis hinge, motor, slider and universal, with range-of-motion limits and a defined breaking behaviour.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Friction and restitution numbers mean different things to different solvers, so agreeing on them buys little and each world may keep its own feel.
note: Bounce, friction coefficients, slip factors, surface speed and two softness terms, with a list naming which of them apply. They attach to the collision collection and to contacts rather than to a surface, which is a different shape of answer from a per-material approach and will not map across one for one.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Two engines producing the same trajectory would let one object be simulated in two places at once, and nothing does that today.
note: The standard accepts that results depend on the machine: it says accuracy depends on the solver implementation and the computing hardware, and it ties evaluation to varying frame times. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for deterministic, repeatable, reproducible and bit-exact on 2026-10-20; the only determinism statements concern event ordering and timer synchronisation, not physics.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Cloth and hair are the visible part, so a moved avatar arrives stiff rather than absent.
note: Only rigid body physics is supported; the softness terms on contacts make surfaces seem somewhat soft but nothing deforms. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for soft body, cloth, deformable and mass-spring on 2026-10-20; no match.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Regions that fire events are part of how content behaves, and their loss makes the content inert rather than unreadable.
note: A proximity sensor fires on entering and leaving a box, with the entry timestamped exactly. It watches the viewer; a separate sensor watches objects. There is no general trigger volume attached to an arbitrary rigid body.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Positioned sounds are authored into a scene, and losing them leaves a silent room.
note: Sound sources include recorded clips, buffers, microphones, oscillators and network streams, each placed in the scene with a location and a direction.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: How direction is turned into sound at the ears is the receiving system's method, like a rendering method.
note: Clause 16 covers spatialized sound and acoustic rendering, with listening points that can sit anywhere and face any direction.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A space's acoustic description is authored with it, and without agreement the room sounds wrong rather than silent.
note: Acoustic properties attach to geometry and colour the sound, and a set of processing nodes including convolution, filtering, delay and compression let a space be given a character.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The receiving runtime works this out from its own geometry, frame by frame.
note: The propagation model covers reflection, refraction and absorption against surrounding geometry, which is most of the physical picture. What is missing is the words themselves: occlusion and obstruction never appear in the clause, and no algorithm is specified for a sound blocked by a wall, so two readers may treat that case differently.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A visitor can be given audio by other means, so disagreement costs quality and scale.
note: There are nodes for a streamed audio source and a streamed audio destination, so the scene can say where live audio enters and leaves. What is missing is the wire: no transport, no codec negotiation and no scale behaviour are specified.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A visitor who cannot be heard is diminished but still present, and text remains a fallback.
note: Live audio enters a scene from a media stream obtained through WebRTC, and can leave through a stream destination, and the distributed simulation component can carry encoded voice in its signal message. Missing: any rule for connecting participants or choosing a voice codec; the standard names the endpoints, not the call.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A client or agent that cannot read the destination's state stream arrives blind, which ends both use cases on the spot.
note: Clause 28 binds a long-standing distributed simulation protocol into the scene, with entity state, transmitter, receiver and signal messages. Two cautions: it shares platform-level simulation entities, not general world state, and it lives in the fullest profile only. It is nonetheless a ratified international standard for sharing state between running instances, which the rest of this map does not have.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Disagreement about who owns an arriving object shows up as rubber-banding and contested edits rather than as a failed arrival.
note: For a shared simulation entity, one node is named the writer and holds the master copy, and every other node is a reader holding a remote copy that the master's messages update. Missing: the clause calls a single owner for each entity "appropriate", which is advice and not a requirement; it covers distributed-simulation entities only, and no authority rule exists for other scene objects or for handing ownership from one node to another.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without agreement the destination sends everything or too little, which costs scale.
note: The only scoping hook is the address and port a node listens on, which the author sets; nothing decides which group a client should join by place or relevance. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for interest, relevance, subscribe, filter and area of interest on 2026-10-20; no interest-management rule found.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Latency hiding is local repair work, so its absence is felt as lag.
note: Entity state messages carry velocity and acceleration and name the dead reckoning algorithm a receiver should apply, which is the prediction half. Missing: any rule for reconciling the prediction with the next authoritative update, such as smoothing or rollback.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: With no shared wire protocol there is no session to join at all.
note: The networking component binds to a wire protocol only for the distributed simulation messages, which it says are typically sent over UDP sockets by multicast, unicast or broadcast, with a field for an RTP header and a unicast relay when wide-area multicast is missing. It is not required for every browser, it covers seven message types, and ordinary scene loading uses plain web addresses; no transport is defined for general world state.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Live audio and video degrade or drop out while the visit continues.
note: Live audio streams can be taken in and sent out through media stream nodes, and the signal message carries audio. Missing: any live video stream node, and any transport, negotiation or scale behaviour for either.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Joining a running world, authentication included, is the door: no agreement, no entry.
note: A node joins a running exercise by setting a network mode and a multicast address and port, and identifies itself with a site, application and entity number, so joining is specified for DIS entities. Missing: any handshake, authentication or admission step; the standard never asks who a joiner is.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: This row is the portal itself, and the travel use case is nothing but the handoff.
note: An anchor node replaces the current world with another one fetched from an address, so plain traversal between worlds is ratified and has been for years. What is missing is everything that should travel with you: no identity, no appearance and no possessions cross the jump.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A roster that does not cross operators means you cannot see who is where, but you can still be there.
note: An entity manager node reports entities that have arrived and entities that have left (by explicit removal or heartbeat timeout), and each entity carries a position, so who is present and where is available within one DIS exercise. Missing: any link to a person or account, and any roster across separate operators beyond the shared exercise.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A destination name that does not resolve cannot be travelled to, so naming and resolution are the first agreement.
note: Addresses name a file on a server, not a live shared place. Two people opening the same address get two independent copies with no connection between them. Nothing resolves a place name into a joinable destination.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Worlds can be reached by a known address, so discovery adds reach rather than making it possible.
note: A scene reaches other content only by an address already written in it (Anchor, Inline, url lists); no directory, registry or announcement of worlds or services is defined. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for discover, registry, directory, lookup, advertise and announce on 2026-10-20; the only hits were the url list search order and unrelated registries.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A shared clock keeps events in order; without one the ordering drifts and coarse clocks still hold the session together.
note: The time half is specified better here than in most of this map. Zero is midnight Greenwich time on 1 January 1970, absolute times are seconds in double precision, a whole clause defines the reader's clock and the nodes that follow it, processing an event at a given time may only produce events at that time or later, and everything in one event cascade carries the same timestamp and is treated as simultaneous. Ordering inside one reader is therefore exact and written down. The shared half is absent. The clock is that reader's own, the one networked clause stamps an arriving message with the moment it reached the local machine, and nothing in the standard agrees a clock between two hosts, estimates the offset between them or orders events across them.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: With no shared base identifier the same person or agent is a stranger in every world they enter.
note: The only base identifiers are the simulation numbers in the networking-for-simulation clause, a site, an application and an entity, valid for the length of one exercise. Missing: any identifier that is globally unique, resolvable or tied to a person, agent or thing outside that exercise.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Claims about age, membership or ownership are worthless if the receiving world cannot read them.
note: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behaviour; how verifiable claims about a subject are expressed is a trust-layer format the scene standard neither performs nor specifies, and carrying a claim as free metadata in a scene would not express it.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A credential nobody can ask for or present is not a credential, and one subject reaches this row natively today.
note: Nothing in the forty-two clauses asks for or presents a credential. The words credential, authentication, certificate, password and authorization do not occur anywhere in this part; permission and privacy occur once each, in a single security sentence on the microphone node that hands the question to the host application. The only identifiers the standard itself defines are simulation numbers in clause 28, a site, an application and an entity, and those are allocation conventions inside one exercise rather than proof of who anyone is. Checked clauses 6 Conformance, 7 Core, 9 Networking including the browser options table, 16 Sound, 28 Distributed interactive simulation and 29 Scripting.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A world that cannot read what an arriving person or agent is allowed to do must either refuse it or trust it blindly.
note: The standard defines scenes and an abstract browser with no notion of a subject holding grants; what a subject may do, readable by an outside party, belongs to an authorization layer, not to this scene format.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without selective disclosure the traveller over-shares, which is a harm rather than a stop.
note: Choosing which attributes of a person to reveal to a receiving world is a function of an identity and credential layer; this scene standard defines what is drawn and heard, not what is disclosed about a subject.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Relationships and standing that do not travel leave the person present but unknown.
note: Portable relationships and standing between people are a social-network service; this standard defines a scene and abstract browser behaviour and has no concept of a person's relationships or reputation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The terms themselves must cross, and that row is a must; acting on them is the receiver's own behaviour, and no agreed mechanism exists yet.
note: Copyright and usage instructions can be written as text in the world information node, but nothing in a browser's required behaviour acts on licence terms when content is used. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for licence, licence terms, rights, enforcement, permission and usage on 2026-10-20; no rule for acting on licence terms found.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Content pinned to the Earth must land in the same place in the other system, and a pose that cannot be read puts it somewhere else.
note: A geographic location node places content at a point on the Earth and orients it to the local frame, with the vertical axis up and one horizontal axis pointing north. Note it defines its own way of saying this rather than referencing the separate pose standard from the geospatial consortium.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A frame disagreement is measured in metres or kilometres, not in taste.
note: Every node that carries geographic coordinates has a field naming its spatial reference frame, with geodetic, transverse mercator and geocentric forms, a table of ellipsoids and a geoid for mean sea level.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: An anchor made on one device never leaves it; the sharing case is the next row.
note: A GeoLocation node fixes any model at a stated geographic position, which one device can use as readily as many, so a scene can place content at a fixed place. Missing: any tie to the device's own tracked space or to a real surface, so the position is only as accurate as the reader's own idea of where it is; this is the same limit as for shared anchors.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Two people in two systems must see the same thing in the same spot, and today one subject reaches this row, through an extension.
note: A location node fixes any model at an absolute geographic position in a stated reference frame, so every device and session that reads the file puts it at the same coordinates. Missing: any way to tie the content to a real surface or to a device's own tracked space, so the position is only as accurate as the reader's own idea of where it is.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Recovering pose from imagery can fall back to satellite position and manual alignment, at worse accuracy.
note: Recovering pose from camera imagery is a sensing service run against a map of the real world; the scope clause leaves physical devices undefined, and the standard places a prepared scene rather than interpreting camera images.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: City-scale data is streamed by tile, and a tileset the receiving client cannot stream has to be converted before it is usable.
note: A terrain level-of-detail node holds up to four child addresses in a quadtree and manages loading and unloading, which is tiled terrain streaming written into an international standard long before the tiled formats in current use.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A structured description of an interior makes placement and routing better; without one both are cruder, and nothing reaches this row today.
note: Geographic positioning, dataset metadata and terrain are specified, but nothing describes the structure of interior spaces such as floors, rooms, openings or connections. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for indoor, building, floor, room, interior and level on 2026-10-20; only unrelated uses found.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The visitor's app and the device runtime are two independent systems, and if they cannot start an immersive session the visit does not happen.
note: The scope clause excludes physical devices, and starting, running and ending a session on a headset is a device and platform contract; the Immersive profile is a named set of components for immersive worlds, not a device session lifecycle.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A world that reads controllers differently is harder to use, and pointer and text paths remain.
note: The scope clause names input devices as outside the standard, so buttons, sticks and pose from handheld controllers are not defined; only abstract pointing and key sensors exist, recorded on the pointing-device row.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Hand tracking adds a way in, and its absence falls back to controllers.
note: The scope clause names input devices as outside the standard, and articulated hand pose from a tracker is a device input; the humanoid component describes a figure to be drawn, not a tracked input source.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Gaze is an aid with privacy limits, and everything works without it.
note: The scope clause names input devices as outside the standard, so gaze direction as a tracked input, and the privacy rules around it, are not defined.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Touch feedback is felt when it is missing, and nothing stops.
note: The scope clause names physical devices as outside the standard, and touch feedback to a user is delivered by a device; no node sends output to a feedback device.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A world that cannot ask what the arriving device can do will guess, and guessing wrong costs quality rather than entry.
note: The companion browser-services part lets a program ask which components a browser supports and ask for its low-level rendering capabilities. Missing: the property names and values are implementation dependent and informational only, so there is no shared vocabulary for what a device can do (input devices, tracking, display), and Part 1 itself has no such service.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The language a world writes its rules in is its own business and never has to cross.
note: Clause 29 defines a script node with an initialize and shutdown lifecycle, event handling and field access. The language bindings themselves live in a companion part of the standard.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The use case says the asset must behave, so a door that will not open in the second system is the failure this row names.
note: Interactivity travels inside the file as a graph of one-way connections between fields, changeable while running, with a defined propagation order. This is a ratified answer to the same question the common asset format is still trying to ratify.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A host can sandbox guest content on its own; agreement only makes the limits predictable for the guest.
note: Some real precautions are written into the text: a model may not include itself, directly or indirectly, and readers are told not to honour such loops; automatic reloading carries an explicit warning. What is missing is everything general. There is no isolation model for scripts, no permission model and no resource budget, so a scene that runs a script is trusting it.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: An agent with no agreed way to perceive and act in a world it did not come from cannot join it at all.
note: A script node can run any program in a scene, but no agent is defined: no identity for it, no way to perceive the world beyond fields, and no rule for what it may do. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for agent, autonomous, AI, bot and NPC on 2026-10-20; no match.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without agreed limits, guest content and agents are throttled or refused unpredictably.
note: Conformance sets limits and minimum requirements for each profile so browsers need not handle unbounded content, and a loop-breaking rule allows each event only once per cascade. Missing: any bound on the time, memory or calls a script may use; the clause says it does not address performance or resource requirements.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: What survives a restart is mostly the host's business; it crosses the boundary only when a visitor's changes must last.
note: Nothing survives a restart because nothing is ever written back. The standard's own list of what an X3D application does covers the world coordinate space, the objects in it, hyperlinks, behaviours and connection to external code, and stops there; there is no store, no save, and no notion of a world that is resumed. The two places the word persistent appears both mean the state of a node's fields while the scene is running, not across a restart. Clause 28 shares live entity state between hosts and keeps none of it. Checked clauses 4 Concepts, 7 Core, 8 Time, 9 Networking, 28 Distributed interactive simulation and 29 Scripting.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The use case names inventory, and items that cannot be read at the destination do not travel with the person.
note: A scene has no concept of a user holding items, and nothing is written back from a running scene to anywhere that outlasts it. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for inventory, item, wallet, owned, belongings, persist, save and store on 2026-10-20; no inventory or carry-over of held objects found.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The use case names preferences, and for a person who depends on comfort and accessibility settings, arriving without them ends the visit.
note: There is one settings vocabulary in the standard and it does not belong to the user. Clause 9.2.4 names nine browser options, among them antialiasing, shading mode, render quality while moving and texture quality, passed in at start-up and held either as parameters on the embedding tag or, in the standard's own words, in an application-specific configuration file or registry entry. Support for them is recommended rather than required, none of them is an accessibility choice, nothing ties a setting to a person, and nothing carries one to another world or another reader. Navigation type, viewpoint and headlight settings in clause 23 belong to the scene, and the reader's own interface for them is explicitly left implementation-dependent. Checked clauses 4 Concepts, 7 Core, 9 Networking, 23 Navigation and 24 Environmental effects.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Naming content by hash makes an item the same item everywhere; without it copies drift while still loading.
note: Content is named by location: url fields hold web addresses and may use name-based resolution through a consortium name space, but no form carries a hash of the content. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for hash, checksum, digest, integrity, fingerprint and content address on 2026-10-20; no match.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A runnable experience moves between hosts far less often than an asset does, and repackaging is the fallback.
note: A runnable scene is a file that points to other files by address; no archive or package that holds a scene with its resources is defined. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for zip, archive, package, bundle and jar on 2026-10-20; the only hit was the packaged shader node, which is one shader file.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Assets reach clients over ordinary web delivery, so agreement here buys scale and cost rather than possibility.
note: Every url field can list several locations that a browser tries in order until one yields usable data, so content can be mirrored. Missing: anything about caching, edge delivery or load at scale.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A reader that cannot tell which version it holds, or what to do with the parts it does not know, breaks on the first update, which is the "no hand fixes" test again.
note: Every file states the version it conforms to, browsers conform per version, and an annex lists for each node which fields each version supports, noting that fields are added in later versions. Missing: a stated rule that a newer reader must accept files written for an older version.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Every other must row is a claim until a shared test says it holds, which is exactly what the meeting asked for.
note: A whole clause on conformance, separately for files, generators and readers, with a base profile that sets minimum requirements and stated aims of eliminating arbitrary subsets and promoting uniform tests. Very little else on this map has this.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: World generation from a prompt or an image
interop_reason: A generated place that arrives only as frames to watch still reaches the viewer, but as a recording rather than a world the receiver can open and use.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and making a whole three-dimensional place from a description or a picture is not an act it performs or specifies.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A world continued by a model still reaches a viewer, but only as what the model chooses to show, so the receiver cannot keep it or run it again.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it never continues a world under a viewer's actions from a learned model; there is no such model here.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: How a system turns photographs into a model is its own method, and what leaves is an ordinary asset the container and geometry rows already carry.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and turning a set of ordinary photographs into a textured three-dimensional model is not among its jobs.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so this row is what geometry encoding is for a mesh: splat content in a named format the receiving tool cannot read does not arrive at all, and re-exporting it is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it names no Gaussian splat interchange format and carries no splat data.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what arrives first, a large capture still loads, it just makes the viewer wait for the whole of it.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it delivers no captured scene, progressively by region and detail or otherwise.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a volumetric clip is an asset like any other: without the calibration and mask metadata a second implementation needs, what arrives is not the recording and no one can make it one by hand.
note: The standard has a volume rendering component, which is the closest any ratified format on this map comes, and it draws a volumetric data set that is already in the scene. It is not a captured, time-varying scene carried as media, and no calibration or mask metadata is defined for one.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a point cloud encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a point cloud, exactly as an undecodable mesh is not a mesh, and that capture shows nothing.
note: The Rendering component defines a point set as a first-class primitive: a set of three-dimensional points in the local coordinate system with a colour at each point. That is the representation and nothing more. There is no compression, no per-point attribute beyond colour, and no import path for the formats a scanner writes.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so views that arrive without their intrinsics and extrinsics cannot be reprojected: the capture lands as loose pictures rather than as the place it recorded.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it carries no set of calibrated camera views with per-pixel depth, and no intrinsics or extrinsics to reproject them.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Making an image from a viewpoint no camera occupied is a method inside one system, and what crosses to a second system is the picture it produced.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it produces no image from a viewing position that no capture camera occupied.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a moving capture handed over as unrelated frames is not the capture: the receiver has to guess the rate and the ordering the sender already knew, and guessing is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it carries no captured scene that changes over time, and states no rate at which one should be played back.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Whether a captured scene answers the light around it is work the receiving system does, and the asset arrives either way.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it holds no captured scene that could be made to answer the light of the place it lands in.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Editing a capture after the fact
interop_reason: Editing a capture happens in the tool that holds it, and what leaves is the edited asset, which the format rows already carry.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and there is no capture here to crop, delete from or recolour, and no export for such an edit to survive.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Describing a change to a world you already made is one service's own interface, and the world that results still leaves by the ordinary export rows.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and there is no generated world here to change by describing the change or pointing at a region.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A generator that cannot read the specification another tool wrote still produces a world, it just will not be the world that was asked for.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and nothing here accepts a specification of a world that should be made.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Deriving conventional assets from a generated scene
interop_reason: Derived meshes and panoramas are how a generated world reaches a conventional engine at all, and each route loses something the receiver has to be told about.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it derives no collision mesh, drawing mesh, panorama or video from a splat or radiance-field world.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Actions that arrive without their embodiment, frame and units cannot be replayed elsewhere, so an agent acts only in the system it was written for.
note: X3D 4.0 is a published international standard for a scene, whose forty-two clauses each define a component, and it carries no agent's actions in or out as time-sampled data with an embodiment, a frame and units.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A panorama whose projection is not stated is still an image, but the receiver has to guess before it can use it as a backdrop or as a light.
note: A 360-degree view of a place is carried, and its projection is stated, but as six images rather than one. The background nodes take back, bottom, front, left, right and top fields, which the standard itself calls a background panorama; a texture background composes the same six sides from texture nodes. Nothing takes a single equirectangular image, which is the form every capture and generation tool on this map produces.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A reconstruction that cannot leave the device that made it keeps the room private to one session, so anything placed against it has to be fitted again elsewhere.
note: A declarative scene graph standard with its own world coordinate system measured in metres. Its nodes describe authored geometry; nothing reads a device's sensors.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Semantic labelling of the real world
interop_reason: Labels each vendor names differently still serve one application, but a second one cannot act on floor or sky without being rewritten for that vendor.
note: The names in an X3D file belong to authored nodes. There is no channel for classes assigned to real surfaces.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Depth reported in units the receiver does not share puts real surfaces at the wrong distance, so content is placed badly rather than not at all.
note: No real-world depth image is defined. Depth in X3D belongs to rendering its own scene.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Whether real surfaces hide virtual content is drawn on the device that sees them, and none of that decision crosses to a second system.
note: The standard composes its own scene; hiding that scene behind real surfaces seen through a camera is outside its architecture.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: How much of the real room a runtime lets through is its own presentation, and an arriving asset cannot tell the difference.
note: X3D 4.0 is a runtime standard with a defined presentation model, so this row is in scope for it, and the model is entirely virtual. The browser draws the scene against a Background node; no node introduces a live camera view of the room and no field controls a blend with one. Checked in the navigation and concepts clauses of the ratified text.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Face and body tracking as input
interop_reason: A face and body stream in a shape the receiver does not read leaves the avatar still rather than absent, and its privacy terms have to be agreed with it.
note: X3D's sensors read pointing devices, keys, time, proximity and collision. The viewer is described to the browser as a size and a speed, not read as a face or a body pose, and there is no live sensor stream of the person to hand to the scene.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A place that arrives without its walkable surface and arrival points still loads, but whoever opens it has to work out where a body may stand and where a portal lands.
note: The strongest declaration of navigable space in any file format on this map, and still only half the row. NavigationInfo carries the avatar's size and the navigation paradigm the browser must present, WALK among them, and Viewpoint nodes give named places a visitor can be put down at, all of it inside the file. What is missing is the walkable surface itself: X3D has no navigation mesh, and the ground a body may stand on is worked out by the browser from Collision and geometry.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A published unit of logic whose name resolves to something else elsewhere still runs, but nobody can be sure which code they called.
note: EXTERNPROTO names a unit of behaviour that lives somewhere else and pulls it in by URL, so an X3D scene really does depend on code published under a name. The name is a web address, not a permanent identity: whoever controls the URL controls what resolves there, and nothing stops a second author reusing a node type name in their own file.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A receiving world that cannot tell what review arriving content has already had still shows it, and has to repeat the whole review itself.
note: X3D defines a software system for running interactive 3D and multimedia content in a browser, with no publishing service, so there is no path between finished content and an audience for a review to stand in.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Two maps of one place with no published transform between them put the same content in two positions, so a person arrives beside where they meant to be.
note: GeoMetadata declares that a geospatial dataset exists and can give its title, valid date range, originator and source address. It has no map version or lifecycle state, and it publishes no transform that aligns one map of a place to another map of the same place.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A service that never declares where it applies still answers, so a client has to call it and find out instead of testing whether it is relevant.
note: The geospatial component's GeoMetadata node can state the bounding coordinates of a dataset in the spatial reference frame named by its coordinateSystem keyword. This is a descriptive keyword in a summary list that a file may omit, it covers content and datasets rather than services, and the standard does not say how a client tests it.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A receiver must distinguish required additions from optional ones or it cannot safely interpret an arriving asset or exchange.
note: PROTO and EXTERNPROTO define named node interfaces and implementation references, with initial-value and event behavior before a required external implementation becomes available.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Named subsets make compatible requirements easier to select, while systems can still agree on the individual requirements without a named profile.
note: X3D 4 defines named profiles, component levels, content declarations and conformance requirements; additional component declarations form an explicit union with the profile.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Content still arrives when color conventions differ, but its colors and brightness can change visibly.
note: One colour space is fixed for the whole standard: RGB with each component from zero to one. Missing: any way to declare a different colour space, a transfer curve or a wider output range on an image, texture or surface, so a receiver has nothing to convert from.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Domain metadata carried with an asset
interop_reason: An asset can load without shared descriptive properties, but receivers lose the classifications and facts that drive its use.
note: The Core component defines typed metadata nodes, names and references, with MetadataSet grouping them for attachment to scene nodes.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Assurance and evidence behind a claim
interop_reason: A credential can be presented without shared assurance detail, but the receiver has less evidence for deciding whether to trust it.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires evidence and assurance information accompanying a claim, enabling the relying party to assess how the claim was established. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A receiving world cannot use a credential reliably unless it can interpret the claim vocabulary and check its structure.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires declaring the vocabulary, types, and validation schemas needed to interpret and check the structure of a claim. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Travel can continue with reusable identifiers, but correlating visits across relationships creates a privacy loss.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires pairwise identifiers and presentation mechanisms that reduce correlation across relationships, with their remaining correlation risks stated. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A moved asset remains usable without a shared preview image, but selection and arrival previews become slower or less informative.
note: Nothing in the standard names a preview image for a file; the header can hold name and value metadata, but no key for an image is defined. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for thumbnail, preview, snapshot, icon, poster and splash on 2026-10-20; the only hits were a style-sheet snapshot reference, a browser splash-screen option and a pointer icon, none a preview of a file.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Travel and participation can use a shared session without encrypted subject payloads, but lack of agreement prevents confidential subject data from following safely.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires identifying recipient key material and algorithms that permit confidential communication or encrypted content for an intended subject. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: After identity keys change, a destination must find the applicable verification material to recognize the same person or agent safely.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires rules for changing, revoking, or recovering identity-control keys and for discovering the applicable verification material. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A destination cannot rely on an issued credential for admission or authority unless the agreed mechanism lets it discover that the credential has been withdrawn.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires a defined mechanism to discover the suspension, revocation, or other status of a credential after issuance. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A scene or visit can continue when interface layouts differ, but carried controls and information may become hard to use.
note: The standard Layout component supplies LayoutGroup/LayoutLayer, dimensions, alignment and world/fraction/pixel units; support depends on the declared component level.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Estimating illumination for the local view stays within the sensing and rendering system and requires no agreement between the independent worlds in the four use cases.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires runtime estimates of environmental illumination made available to content for lighting or reflections. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Shared marker references improve physical alignment across systems, while a scene or visit can still proceed with another placement method.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires detecting recognized physical markers or images and reporting their tracked pose relative to a runtime reference space. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: An asset with external resources cannot load intact if the receiver cannot resolve its resource references in the intended context.
note: EXTERNPROTO resolves ordered resource URLs and fragment-named prototype definitions into the required external scene implementation; this is a specified resource-resolution operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Pose series and live pose streams
interop_reason: Systems exchanging moving subjects must agree on the time and frame of each pose or the subject's movement cannot be reconstructed correctly.
note: X3D's EnvironmentalSensor component reports timestamped position and orientation changes through ProximitySensor events. These are pose streams in the scene's local coordinate context.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Turning local pointing input into a scene hit stays inside the receiving application and does not require agreement between independent worlds.
note: PointingDeviceSensor nodes expose intersection point, normal and texture-coordinate events for pointed scene geometry; the browser supplies the pointing device.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Receiving text through a local input field or keyboard interface is a device-side interaction and need not be shared between worlds.
note: The KeyDeviceSensor component defines StringSensor character/string entry events independently of controller action interpretation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: The choice of image layers sent to a device compositor is local presentation work and need not be shared across a world boundary.
note: The layering component gives an ordered set of independent layers, each with its own viewpoint and navigation and a viewport that confines it to a sub-region of the display, composed in the stated order. Missing: layers that are images with their own shape, pose and blending properties handed to a compositor; the layers here are sub-scenes.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Shared bounds let a receiver select content before loading its geometry; without them the content can still move but loads and traverses less efficiently.
note: Grouping nodes carry hierarchical bounding boxes for traversal and rejection; unspecified bounds are treated as unbounded, so pruning depends on correctly authored bounds.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Losing agreed object sets weakens grouped scene operations while the individual objects can still be transferred and rendered.
note: DEF-named Group nodes define sets of child objects with addChildren/removeChildren operations and group-level targets; rule-based membership expressions are not required for this named-set support.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A moved object or avatar can still load when constraints are lost, but linked movement and pose behavior degrade.
note: The billboard node turns its children about an axis to face the viewer, rigid body joints constrain one body's motion to another, and any field can be routed to another node's field, so some relationships between transforms can be authored. Missing: a general constraint node that drives one node's transform from another with stated evaluation order, such as aim, parent or follow.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A scene can transfer without agreed media timing, but its video, sound and coordinated presentation can be lost or drift.
note: AudioClip and Sound reference audiovisual-scene audio with start/stop/loop timing; the Time and Texturing components separately define timed MovieTexture presentation in the same event model.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Physical play-area bounds and floor references describe one device's surroundings and can remain local while the four cross-system use cases proceed.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. This row requires runtime-reported physical play-area bounds and floor-relative reference information available to an application. That function belongs to a different layer than this subject's declared function; supplying data to such a system does not perform or specify the operation.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A moved scene remains usable without its agreed synthesis model, but generated sound and its response to changing controls are lost.
note: The Sound component exchanges OscillatorSource and PeriodicWave nodes with waveform coefficients and changing frequency/gain controls, producing audio at playback time.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A receiver cannot access protected transferred content unless it can identify the protection mechanism required for that content.
note: Part 1 declares no protection scheme. The companion compressed binary encoding optionally applies XML encryption to scene fragments, so a protected fragment can be recognised as encrypted by that mechanism. Missing: a declaration in the scene itself that names the scheme or the key arrangement a recipient needs. Searched Part 1 of ISO/IEC 19775-1 version 4.0, all component clauses and annexes, for encrypt, protection scheme, DRM and signature on 2026-10-20; the only hits were radio encryption fields in the simulation component and unrelated node-signature wording, so no protection declaration is defined in Part 1. The XML encryption specification itself was not read.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Without agreed links and transform meaning, receivers cannot reconstruct the same related frames for transferred content or participants.
note: The grouping and Transform hierarchy exchanges related coordinate frames with a defined parent/child transform model; this covers transform trees, without claiming arbitrary constraint-graph solvers.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: Travel and participation can continue without shared zone-event meaning, but spatial notifications and summaries lose useful context.
note: Sensor nodes define a box region and send typed events when the viewer or a target object enters, leaves or moves inside it, and each node can be named in the file. Missing: a way to interchange identified zones as data separate from a scene, and any summary of events with defined spatial and temporal meaning.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
interop_reason: A recipient that cannot interpret the carried permission cannot determine whether the requested use of the subject or data is authorized.
note: The standard describes scene content and abstract browser behaviour, and consent with scope, purpose, validity and withdrawal is a governance record about people or data; the one nearby sentence, on the microphone node, leaves permission to the host application.

subject: X3D (ISO/IEC 19775-1)
capability: Record of what a system decided
interop_reason: A shared evaluation receipt makes cross-system actions auditable, while travel or participation can still occur without that record.
note: The subject reviewed here is scoped as follows: X3D 4 specifies interactive multimedia scenes and abstract browser behavior, with physical device implementation excluded. interop_reason: The use case says the asset must behave, so a door that will not open in the second system is the failure this row names.

subject: glTF

subject: glTF
interop_reason: The use case names inventory, and items that cannot be read at the destination do not travel with the person.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: The use case names preferences, and for a person who depends on comfort and accessibility settings, arriving without them ends the visit.

interop_reason: A runnable experience moves between hosts far less often than an asset does, and repackaging is the fallback.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Assets reach clients over ordinary web delivery, so agreement here buys scale and cost rather than possibility.

subject: glTF

note: Three separate mechanisms: a file version, a minimum version a reader must support, and lists of extensions used against extensions required, so a reader knows in advance whether it can load the file at all.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Every other must row is a claim until a shared test says it holds, which is exactly what the meeting asked for.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so this row is what geometry encoding is for a mesh: splat content in a named format the receiving tool cannot read does not arrive at all, and re-exporting it is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: KHR_gaussian_splatting is ratified, and it is the one named way splat data travels in glTF: position, rotation, scale, opacity and spherical harmonics stored as attributes on a point primitive, with a required kernel and colour space. subject: glTF
interop_reason: Without an agreed order for what arrives first, a large capture still loads, it just makes the viewer wait for the whole of it.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a volumetric clip is an asset like any other: without the calibration and mask metadata a second implementation needs, what arrives is not the recording and no one can make it one by hand.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a point cloud encoded in a way the receiver cannot decode is not a point cloud, exactly as an undecodable mesh is not a mesh, and that capture shows nothing.
note: A mesh primitive may use point topology, so a plain set of points travels in the core, and the splat extension leans on exactly that fallback. What the core does not define is any point-cloud compression or the per-point attribute set a capture pipeline produces, so a lidar or photogrammetry point cloud arrives as ordinary vertex attributes and nothing states what they mean.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so views that arrive without their intrinsics and extrinsics cannot be reprojected: the capture lands as loose pictures rather than as the place it recorded.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Making an image from a viewpoint no camera occupied is a method inside one system, and what crosses to a second system is the picture it produced.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Captured content is first-class, so a moving capture handed over as unrelated frames is not the capture: the receiver has to guess the rate and the ordering the sender already knew, and guessing is the hand fix the use case forbids.
note: The core animates authored nodes, skins and morph targets against a timeline. It carries no captured scene that changes over time, and the splat extension is static: a Gaussian set has no time axis, so a moving capture has to be handed over as unrelated files.

subject: glTF
interop_reason: Whether a captured scene answers the light around it is work the receiving system does, and the asset arrives either way.

A receiver may therefore relight, and two receivers will not agree.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Friction and restitution numbers mean different things to different solvers, so agreeing on them buys little and each world may keep its own feel.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Cloth and hair are the visible part, so a moved avatar arrives stiff rather than absent.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Regions that fire events are part of how content behaves, and their loss makes the content inert rather than unreadable.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Positioned sounds are authored into a scene, and losing them leaves a silent room.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: A space's acoustic description is authored with it, and without agreement the room sounds wrong rather than silent.

interop_reason: The receiving runtime works this out from its own geometry, frame by frame.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Disagreement about who owns an arriving object shows up as rubber-banding and contested edits rather than as a failed arrival.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Without agreement the destination sends everything or too little, which costs scale.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: A roster that does not cross operators means you cannot see who is where, but you can still be there.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: With no shared base identifier the same person or agent is a stranger in every world they enter.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Claims about age, membership or ownership are worthless if the receiving world cannot read them.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: A credential nobody can ask for or present is not a credential, and one subject reaches this row natively today.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Without selective disclosure the traveller over-shares, which is a harm rather than a stop.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

interop_reason: An anchor made on one device never leaves it; the sharing case is the next row.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Two people in two systems must see the same thing in the same spot, and today one subject reaches this row, through an extension.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: Recovering pose from imagery can fall back to satellite position and manual alignment, at worse accuracy.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: City-scale data is streamed by tile, and a tileset the receiving client cannot stream has to be converted before it is usable.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: The visitor's app and the device runtime are two independent systems, and if they cannot start an immersive session the visit does not happen.

subject: Meta Horizon Hyperscape Capture
interop_reason: A world that reads controllers differently is harder to use, and pointer and text paths remain.
